<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

An opt-in decode path for GLM-5.2 (`glm_moe_dsa`, MXFP4 experts) at TP8 on MI355X (gfx950). It runs each MoE decoder layer (3..77) as one persistent FlyDSL kernel, in "layer mode", inside the stock layer loop.

It uses the `SpecializedDecode` interface of #61867 (Kimi-K3, merged):
- the switch is `additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}`;
- the model refuses unsupported deployments at startup;
- a `ModelState` builds and binds the executor;
- `plan()` runs once per step.

RFC: #60904.

**Related work, and why this isn't a duplicate.** Checked with `gh pr list --state open --search "GLM-5.2 monokernel"` / `"GLM 5.2 decode ROCm"` and against the RFC thread.

| PR | What it is | How it relates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #61867 (merged) | Kimi-K3 SpecializedDecode, NVIDIA | Same interface and the same batch-size approach; this is the first AMD user of it, for a different model |
| #60397 (merged) | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode, MI355X | Different model and kernels |
| #61482, #60731, #60683, #61662 (open) | DSv4-Pro, DSv4.1 on gfx942, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm | Different models; nothing shared with GLM-5.2's DSA + MXFP4 MoE layer |
| #61311 (open) | Shared specialized-decode abstractions | This PR keeps its runtime per model, as #61867 does, and can move onto shared helpers if those land |

No other PR targets GLM-5.2 decode kernels.

## Claims

- **Speed:** decode TPOT falls by 2.30× at batch 1 and 1.51× at batch 8 on 8× MI355X, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, 3000-token prompts, FULL decode graphs.
- **Accuracy:** at parity with stock on GSM8K (5-shot, greedy, n=1319).
- **Weights:** served at the checkpoint's precision, read in place from vLLM's loaded modules. Nothing is re-quantized at load time.
  - BF16-attention checkpoints (`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`) run BF16 attention, and vLLM's indexer refreshes the indexer layers. Validated on GPU.
  - Checkpoints that ship Quark per-channel FP8 attention (`amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) run FP8 attention units with the checkpoint's per-row scales. With `max_model_len` ≤ 4096 they also run the indexer fused into the kernel. Validated on GPU (results below).
- **Supported configurations:** listed in `specialized_decode/README.md`, which grows as support is added.
- **Stock path unchanged:** without the switch, `specialized_decode_config()` returns `None`, and the model, model state and layer loop behave exactly as before.
- **Refusal at startup:** if you set the switch on a deployment it can't serve, startup fails with one `ValueError` that names every unsupported setting.

## Validation

**Performance.** TPOT in ms on current main, offline `LLM`, TP8, prompt 3000 tokens, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs. Each cell is the mean of 3 runs.

| Configuration | Batch 1 | Batch 8 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock (`decode_backend=auto`) | 13.69 (13.68–13.69) | 17.47 (17.19–17.79) |
| Specialized decode | **5.94** (5.94–5.95) | **11.57** (11.52–11.66) |

**Model evaluation.** GSM8K, 5-shot (the first 5 train exemplars), greedy, `max_tokens=256`, all 1319 test questions, FULL graphs.

| Configuration | Strict | Flexible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Specialized decode | 1247 (94.5% ± 0.6) | 1249 |
| Stock, same harness (earlier base) | 1218–1230 | |

> The table and GSM8K come from the previous revision of this PR configured as this revision's defaults (BF16 attention, `indexer_mode="indexer_only"`); the compiled kernels are byte-identical.

**This revision with vLLM's default capture sizes** (`max_num_seqs=32`, no `cudagraph_capture_sizes` set). Captured graphs up to 8 run the kernels; 16 and above capture vLLM's decode.

| Batch | 1 | 3 (pads to 4) | 8 | 16 (stock graph) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TPOT (ms) | 5.94 | 8.36 | 11.57 | 20.85 (stock alone: 20.77) |

GSM8K with batch sizes 10 and 12 also built and in use (limit raised to 12 for the run, `max_num_seqs=12`): 1236/1319 strict.

**FP8-attention checkpoint** (`amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, fused indexer), against vLLM on the same checkpoint. TPOT in ms, same setup, mean of 3 runs.

| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 14.48 | 15.24 | 15.85 | 16.68 | 17.40 | 18.23 | 19.39 |
| Specialized decode | **4.89** | 5.98 | 7.34 | 8.74 | **10.27** | 14.83 | 17.24 |
| Speedup | 2.96× | 2.55× | 2.16× | 1.91× | 1.69× | 1.23× | 1.12× |

- **Batch 8:** the middle value is shown; the three runs were 10.27, 10.27 and 11.88.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K strict is 1230/1319 for the specialized decode and 1226 for stock on the same checkpoint.
- **What vLLM loads:** vLLM selects `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` for the attention linears. The specialized decode reads those preshuffled FP8 weights and per-row scales without re-quantizing, and logs `FP8 per-channel attention (checkpoint precision); fused indexer on 18 indexer layers`.

**Batch-size sweep, BF16** (why `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is 8). TPOT in ms, 3000-token prompts, FULL graphs, mean of 3 runs. Built up to 12 for the sweep; 16 and 24 run vLLM's graphs.

| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 16 | 24 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 13.71 | 14.71 | 15.52 | 16.59 | 17.38 | 18.44 | 19.51 | 20.77 | 24.80 |
| Specialized decode | 5.94 | 6.81 | 8.46 | 10.13 | 11.55 | 14.84 | 18.41 | 20.80 | 24.79 |
| Speedup | 2.31× | 2.16× | 1.83× | 1.64× | 1.50× | 1.24× | 1.06× | 1.00× | 1.00× |

- **Above 8 the kernel slows sharply.** Each extra request costs about 0.8 ms up to 8, then about 1.7 ms per request from 8 to 12, as the kernel moves to a second row group.
- **Throughput peaks at batch 8**, at 693 tok/s; batch 12 gives 652. The FP8 checkpoint falls off the same way above 8, so the limit is 8 for both.

**Other end-to-end checks**
- Eager and FULL-graph runs at batch 1 and 4 give coherent text.
- The executor reports the kernels ran on the decode steps.
- An unsupported deployment fails at startup on every rank with one message, e.g. `does not support: the V1 model runner (set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1) (decode_backend=auto runs vLLM's decode)`.

**Reproduce**
```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <GLM-5.2-MXFP4> -tp 8 \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

**Tests run**
```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/deepseek_v32
#   69 passed, 2 skipped (the 2 FlyDSL kernel-build tests skip without a gfx950 toolchain;
#   both pass in a compile-only gfx950 container)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all hooks pass, incl. mypy and test tethering
```

**CI coverage.** A new Buildkite step, `:amd: (MI355) GLM-5.2 Specialized Decode` (`mi355_1`), runs the tests above. End-to-end coverage isn't possible in CI because it needs the GLM-5.2 checkpoint on 8 GPUs. The end-to-end runs above were done locally on 8× MI355X.

## Details

**Shape.** Layer mode of the #61867 interface:
- `specialized_decode_config()` runs in `__init__`, before any weights are allocated.
- `DeepseekV32ModelState` builds the executor after the weights load, and calls `prepare_kv()` from `ModelState.initialize_kv_cache` at every KV bind.
- `forward()` calls `plan()` once per step. It returns a `Step` only for plain decode steps the kernels serve, and the layer loop then asks `step.layer(i)` for a kernel. Prefill and mixed batches run the stock layers unchanged.
- The kernel reads vLLM's loaded weights and its KV and index caches in place. There is no second weight copy or checkpoint re-read.

**Batch sizes.** This follows #61867's approach.
- Two constants in `specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py` set the limit:
  - `BATCH_SIZES = (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)` is what the kernel can be built for;
  - `MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 8`, set from the sweep above.
- The kernels are built for the batch sizes up to 8: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8. A smaller batch pads up to the next of these (3 runs as 4).
- A step with at most 8 requests runs the kernels; a larger one runs vLLM's decode.
- Larger batches run vLLM's decode.
- Capture sizes and `max_num_seqs` aren't restricted. FULL graphs above 8 capture vLLM's decode. The startup log says `layers 3..77, batch sizes (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8); larger batches run vLLM's decode`.

**Unsupported, refused at startup**
- model_type other than `glm_moe_dsa`; TP≠8; PP, DP, EP, DCP, PCP or DBO;
- speculative decoding, sleep mode, LoRA, KV-transfer connectors, routed-expert capture;
- AITER fused shared experts;
- dtype other than bf16; `kv_cache_dtype` other than auto/bf16;
- MRV1; `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`;
- not gfx950;
- malformed `specialized_decode` options; `step_sync` under FULL graphs.

**FP8-attention checkpoints**
- The path is chosen from the loaded weights, with no option to set:
  - all four attention matrices FP8 per-channel gives FP8 attention;
  - FP8 `wq_b` and `max_model_len` ≤ 4096 add the fused indexer.
- Partial or mixed FP8, and block, per-tensor or non-Quark FP8, are refused.
- vLLM's FP8 GEMM layouts, including AITER's (16,16) preshuffle, are undone by byte permutation only.
- The BF16 kernels compile to byte-identical code with this change. The FP8 + fused-indexer kernels build at every batch size with no VGPR spills.

**Checked later**
- When the executor is built: the MoE layout and backend, BF16 attention weights (a checkpoint with quantized attention is refused here), and the RoPE table.
- At each KV bind: the caches are bound and contiguous, use the MLA row layout, and are under 4 GiB.

**Core components and complexity**
- No core files are touched. Outside the new directories, the only changes are `amd/model.py` +60/−1, `amd/model_state.py` +21 (new) and one Buildkite step.
- New code: about 1.5k lines of runtime (`specialized_decode/runtime/`), 3.7k lines of vendored FlyDSL kernel (`specialized_decode/flydsl/`, JIT-compiled, no binaries, ruff-clean without excludes) and 1.5k lines of tests.

**MRV2 only.** The path is built on MRV2's `ModelState` hooks. With MRV1, startup is refused with the reason, since this architecture still defaults to MRV1 on ROCm.

**Tradeoffs and limitations**
- Only plain decode at batch sizes up to 8 is accelerated, which is the latency-serving case.
- **Host syncs:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` stops at `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:726`, in vLLM's ROCm sparse-MLA metadata builder, and stock vLLM stops at the same line. With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` on the same workload (batch 1 and 8), stock logs 384 `synchronize` calls and the specialized decode 352, so the specialized decode adds none of its own.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - FP8-attention checkpoints (e.g. `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), including the fused indexer;
  - MTP, which is refused for now;
  - TP other than 8, and other GPUs.

**Interactions with open PRs**
- **#61941** turns AITER fused shared experts on by default for GLM-5.x MXFP4. This path refuses that setting, so once #61941 lands, users of this switch must turn the fusion off. Alternatively the kernel could learn that layout.
- **#61985** adds an MXFP4 indexer K cache, which needs a refusal or kernel support before it becomes the default.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to write and refactor parts of this change, run the validation and draft this description.

---

Would an alternative be to set timeouts on every rank and let each rank raise if exceeded, and also have a timeout on the poller? I.e. if one rank hangs, it will timeout and raise, and thus not participate in the collective and hence after a subsequent timeout all ranks will raise.

+"""Build-time checks and the poll-error fail-stop of the GLM-5.2 specialized decode
+(the config-only checks are ``runtime.unsupported``, the KV-bind checks
+``MonoLayers.bind_caches``).
+
+Build (``SpecializedDecode.__init__``): vLLM's RoPE cache covers max_model_len. Per step
+(``PollErrorWatch``): a non-blocking, one-step-delayed fail-stop on expired kernel
+polls, so the engine fails instead of serving wrong tokens."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def check_rope_table(backbone, cfg) -> None:
+    """VLLM's cos_sin_cache covers the kernel's RoPE table (cfg.max_model_len >= vLLM's
+    max_model_len, see ``runtime.decode_config``)."""
+    rows = backbone.layers[cfg.layers[0]].self_attn.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache.shape[0]
+    if rows < cfg.max_model_len:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"GLM-5.2 specialized decode: vLLM's cos_sin_cache has {rows} rows < "
+            f"max_model_len {cfg.max_model_len}"
+        )
+
+
+# the output rank's first fail-stop message (None until one fires)
+_FAILED: dict[str, str | None] = dict(msg=None)
+# seconds the output rank lives on after its fail-stop, for the raised error to reach
+# the engine through the worker's RPC reply
+FAILSTOP_EXIT_GRACE_S = 5.0
+
+
+def _fail_hard(msg: str):
+    """Terminate this worker: a non-output TP rank's exception never reaches the
+    engine, so raising would let the other ranks keep emitting tokens."""
+    logger.critical("%s -> terminating this worker (non-output rank)", msg)
+    os._exit(70)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 14.48 | 15.24 | 15.85 | 16.68 | 17.40 | 18.23 | 19.39 |
| Specialized decode | **4.89** | 5.98 | 7.34 | 8.74 | **10.27** | 14.83 | 17.24 |
| Speedup | 2.96× | 2.55× | 2.16× | 1.91× | 1.69× | 1.23× | 1.12× |

- **Batch 8:** the middle value is shown; the three runs were 10.27, 10.27 and 11.88.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K strict is 1230/1319 for the specialized decode and 1226 for stock on the same checkpoint.
- **What vLLM loads:** vLLM selects `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel` for the attention linears. The specialized decode reads those preshuffled FP8 weights and per-row scales without re-quantizing, and logs `FP8 per-channel attention (checkpoint precision); fused indexer on 18 indexer layers`.

**Batch-size sweep, BF16** (why `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is 8). TPOT in ms, 3000-token prompts, FULL graphs, mean of 3 runs. Built up to 12 for the sweep; 16 and 24 run vLLM's graphs.

| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 16 | 24 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock | 13.71 | 14.71 | 15.52 | 16.59 | 17.38 | 18.44 | 19.51 | 20.77 | 24.80 |
| Specialized decode | 5.94 | 6.81 | 8.46 | 10.13 | 11.55 | 14.84 | 18.41 | 20.80 | 24.79 |
| Speedup | 2.31× | 2.16× | 1.83× | 1.64× | 1.50× | 1.24× | 1.06× | 1.00× | 1.00× |

- **Above 8 the kernel slows sharply.** Each extra request costs about 0.8 ms up to 8, then about 1.7 ms per request from 8 to 12, as the kernel moves to a second row group.
- **Throughput peaks at batch 8**, at 693 tok/s; batch 12 gives 652. The FP8 checkpoint falls off the same way above 8, so the limit is 8 for both.

**Other end-to-end checks**
- Eager and FULL-graph runs at batch 1 and 4 give coherent text.
- The executor reports the kernels ran on the decode steps.
- An unsupported deployment fails at startup on every rank with one message, e.g. `does not support: the V1 model runner (set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1) (decode_backend=auto runs vLLM's decode)`.

**Reproduce**
```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <GLM-5.2-MXFP4> -tp 8 \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

**Tests run**
```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/deepseek_v32
#   69 passed, 2 skipped (the 2 FlyDSL kernel-build tests skip without a gfx950 toolchain;
#   both pass in a compile-only gfx950 container)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # all hooks pass, incl. mypy and test tethering
```

**CI coverage.** A new Buildkite step, `:amd: (MI355) GLM-5.2 Specialized Decode` (`mi355_1`), runs the tests above. End-to-end coverage isn't possible in CI because it needs the GLM-5.2 checkpoint on 8 GPUs. The end-to-end runs above were done locally on 8× MI355X.

## Details

**Shape.** Layer mode of the #61867 interface:
- `specialized_decode_config()` runs in `__init__`, before any weights are allocated.
- `DeepseekV32ModelState` builds the executor after the weights load, and calls `prepare_kv()` from `ModelState.initialize_kv_cache` at every KV bind.
- `forward()` calls `plan()` once per step. It returns a `Step` only for plain decode steps the kernels serve, and the layer loop then asks `step.layer(i)` for a kernel. Prefill and mixed batches run the stock layers unchanged.
- The kernel reads vLLM's loaded weights and its KV and index caches in place. There is no second weight copy or checkpoint re-read.

**Batch sizes.** This follows #61867's approach.
- Two constants in `specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py` set the limit:
  - `BATCH_SIZES = (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)` is what the kernel can be built for;
  - `MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 8`, set from the sweep above.
- The kernels are built for the batch sizes up to 8: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8. A smaller batch pads up to the next of these (3 runs as 4).
- A step with at most 8 requests runs the kernels; a larger one runs vLLM's decode.
- Larger batches run vLLM's decode.
- Capture sizes and `max_num_seqs` aren't restricted. FULL graphs above 8 capture vLLM's decode. The startup log says `layers 3..77, batch sizes (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8); larger batches run vLLM's decode`.

**Unsupported, refused at startup**
- model_type other than `glm_moe_dsa`; TP≠8; PP, DP, EP, DCP, PCP or DBO;
- speculative decoding, sleep mode, LoRA, KV-transfer connectors, routed-expert capture;
- AITER fused shared experts;
- dtype other than bf16; `kv_cache_dtype` other than auto/bf16;
- MRV1; `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`;
- not gfx950;
- malformed `specialized_decode` options; `step_sync` under FULL graphs.

**FP8-attention checkpoints**
- The path is chosen from the loaded weights, with no option to set:
  - all four attention matrices FP8 per-channel gives FP8 attention;
  - FP8 `wq_b` and `max_model_len` ≤ 4096 add the fused indexer.
- Partial or mixed FP8, and block, per-tensor or non-Quark FP8, are refused.
- vLLM's FP8 GEMM layouts, including AITER's (16,16) preshuffle, are undone by byte permutation only.
- The BF16 kernels compile to byte-identical code with this change. The FP8 + fused-indexer kernels build at every batch size with no VGPR spills.

**Checked later**
- When the executor is built: the MoE layout and backend, BF16 attention weights (a checkpoint with quantized attention is refused here), and the RoPE table.
- At each KV bind: the caches are bound and contiguous, use the MLA row layout, and are under 4 GiB.

**Core components and complexity**
- No core files are touched. Outside the new directories, the only changes are `amd/model.py` +60/−1, `amd/model_state.py` +21 (new) and one Buildkite step.
- New code: about 1.5k lines of runtime (`specialized_decode/runtime/`), 3.7k lines of vendored FlyDSL kernel (`specialized_decode/flydsl/`, JIT-compiled, no binaries, ruff-clean without excludes) and 1.5k lines of tests.

**MRV2 only.** The path is built on MRV2's `ModelState` hooks. With MRV1, startup is refused with the reason, since this architecture still defaults to MRV1 on ROCm.

**Tradeoffs and limitations**
- Only plain decode at batch sizes up to 8 is accelerated, which is the latency-serving case.
- **Host syncs:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` stops at `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:726`, in vLLM's ROCm sparse-MLA metadata builder, and stock vLLM stops at the same line. With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` on the same workload (batch 1 and 8), stock logs 384 `synchronize` calls and the specialized decode 352, so the specialized decode adds none of its own.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - FP8-attention checkpoints (e.g. `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), including the fused indexer;
  - MTP, which is refused for now;
  - TP other than 8, and other GPUs.

**Interactions with open PRs**
- **#61941** turns AITER fused shared experts on by default for GLM-5.x MXFP4. This path refuses that setting, so once #61941 lands, users of this switch must turn the fusion off. Alternatively the kernel could learn that layout.
- **#61985** adds an MXFP4 indexer K cache, which needs a refusal or kernel support before it becomes the default.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to write and refactor parts of this change, run the validation and draft this description.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CPU / torch golden model of vLLM's GLM-5.2 decode indexer path on ROCm gfx950.
+
+One decode step, T rows (one token per request), from the indexer layer's normed input
+``h`` to the CSR physical slot list the MonoKernel consumes. Each stage names the vLLM
+code it mirrors:
+
+ 1. q_c = bf16(rms_norm(bf16(h @ W_qa[:q_lora]^T), w_qa_norm, eps))
+      fused_qkv_a_proj q rows; fused_norm_rope program 2 (_rms_norm), bf16 q_c_out
+ 2. iq = bf16(q_c @ W_qb^T).view(T, 32, 128)
+      indexer.wq_b
+ 3. iq = rope_interleave(iq[..., :64], pos); (iq_fp8, s_q) = ue8m0_fp8(iq) per
+    (row, head)
+      _fused_q_kernel program 1 (fused_q; INDEX_ROPE_INTERLEAVE for GLM-5.2)
+ 4. w = float(kw[:, 128:]) * s_q * head_dim^-0.5 * n_head^-0.5
+      same program ("index weights update")
+ 5. k = layer_norm(float(kw[:, :128]), w_k, b_k, 1e-6); rope_interleave(k[:64], pos);
+    (k_fp8, s_k) = ue8m0_fp8(k), written at ``slot`` into the uint8 [blocks, 16, 132]
+    index cache in the SHUFFLE layout
+      fused_norm_rope program 0 + _fp8_quant_and_cache_write;
+      kw = bf16(h @ W_wk^T) = indexer.wk_weights_proj ([wk (128) | weights_proj (32)])
+ 6. logits[r, t] = s_k[t] * sum_h w[r, h] * relu(iq_fp8[r, h] . k_fp8[t]),
+    t < seq_len[r]
+      fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch (v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py); the
+      production deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits computes the same sum in another order
+ 7. top-k: torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_decode (radix histogram select)
+      seq_len <= 2048: indices 0..L-1 in order, then -1; else an exact top-2048 SET by
+      value in a nondeterministic order, threshold ties taken in arrival order, values
+      compared by float bits (-0.0 < +0.0). ``topk_ref`` returns the canonical choice
+      (lowest index among threshold ties) plus the tie set, so comparisons are
+      set-equality modulo threshold ties.
+ 8. CSR: indptr = cumsum(min(seq_len, 2048)) (generate_sparse_seqlen_kernel);
+    indices[indptr[r] + i] = bt[r, tok // 16] * 16 + tok % 16, or 0 for tok < 0 or an
+    out-of-range block (triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index)
+
+Bit-faithfulness: stages 3-5 (RoPE, ue8m0 FP8, cache bytes) follow the Triton op order
+in fp32 and are expected bit-exact for bit-identical inputs (Triton may contract
+a*c + s*p into an FMA; a 1-ulp difference flips an FP8 rounding only at exact
+midpoints). The bf16 GEMMs (1, 2, 5) and the logits (6) accumulate in a different order
+than the GPU, so compare them with tolerances; the top-k set is then exact except where
+two logits differ by less than the logits error at the threshold.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+
+FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn  # gfx950: OCP E4M3 (USE_FNUZ False), FP8_MAX 448
+FP8_MAX = 448.0
+BLOCK = 16  # GLM-5.2 vLLM block size (index cache block == MLA block)
+HEAD_DIM = 128  # index_head_dim
+N_HEAD = 32  # index_n_heads
+ROPE = 64  # qk_rope_head_dim (index rope covers dims [0, 64), interleaved pairs)
+TOPK = 2048
+# _INDEXER_CACHE_BLOCK_TILE (tokens) == _INDEXER_CACHE_HEAD_TILE_BYTES (bytes), fp8
+TILE = 16
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ elementwise stages
+def bf16(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return x.to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def rms_norm(x, w, eps):
+    x = x.float()
+    rrms = torch.rsqrt((x * x).sum(-1, keepdim=True) / x.shape[-1] + eps)
+    return (x * rrms) * w.float()
+
+
+def layer_norm(x, w, b, eps):
+    x = x.float()
+    mean = x.sum(-1, keepdim=True) / x.shape[-1]
+    diff = x - mean
+    var = (diff * diff).sum(-1, keepdim=True) / x.shape[-1]
+    rstd = torch.rsqrt(var + eps)
+    return (x - mean) * rstd * w.float() + b.float()
+
+
+def rope_interleave(
+    x: torch.Tensor, cos_sin: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """X [..., D] fp32 with the row axis first; pairs (2i, 2i+1), i < ROPE/2, rotated by
+    cos_sin[pos] = [cos | sin] (kernels.py: roped = x * cos_full + sign * partner *
+    sin_full, sign -1 on even lanes)."""
+    half = cos_sin.shape[-1] // 2
+    cs = cos_sin[pos.long()].float()
+    shape = (x.shape[0],) + (1,) * (x.dim() - 2) + (half,)
+    c, s = cs[:, :half].reshape(shape), cs[:, half:].reshape(shape)
+    out = x.clone()
+    e, o = x[..., 0 : 2 * half : 2], x[..., 1 : 2 * half : 2]
+    out[..., 0 : 2 * half : 2] = e * c + (-o) * s
+    out[..., 1 : 2 * half : 2] = o * c + e * s
+    return out
+
+
+def ue8m0_fp8(v: torch.Tensor, exact: bool = False):
+    """_fp8_ue8m0_quantize over the last dim: scale = 2^ceil(log2(max(amax, 1e-4) /
+    448)); q = fp8(v / scale). exact=False: fp32 log2 as vLLM / torch evaluate it -- for
+    x = amax/448 a few ulps above a power of two the fp32 log2 rounds to that integer,
+    so the scale is 2^k and amax/scale slightly exceeds 448 (E4M3 RN brings it back to
+    448). exact=True: the mathematically exact ceil (exponent bits + mantissa != 0),
+    which the fused kernel's _ue8m0_scale computes (flydsl/glm/kernel.py); the two
+    differ by 2x in that window only."""
+    v = v.float()
+    amax = v.abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True)
+    x = torch.clamp(amax, min=1e-4) / FP8_MAX
+    if exact:
+        bits = x.contiguous().view(torch.int32)
+        e = ((bits >> 23) & 255) + ((bits & 0x7FFFFF) != 0).to(torch.int32)
+        scale = (e << 23).view(torch.float32)
+    else:
+        scale = torch.exp2(torch.ceil(torch.log2(x)))
+    return (v / scale).to(FP8), scale.squeeze(-1)
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ index cache
+def value_offset(block_offset: int | torch.Tensor, d: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """SHUFFLE layout byte offset inside a block (kernels.py
+    _fp8_quant_and_cache_write): [blk/16, D/16, 16 tokens, 16 bytes]."""
+    return (
+        block_offset // TILE * TILE * HEAD_DIM
+        + block_offset % TILE * TILE
+        + d // TILE * TILE * TILE
+        + d % TILE
+    )
+
+
+def cache_write(cache: torch.Tensor, slot: int, k_fp8: torch.Tensor, scale: float):
+    blk, off = slot // BLOCK, slot % BLOCK
+    flat = cache.view(cache.shape[0], -1)
+    flat[blk, value_offset(off, torch.arange(HEAD_DIM))] = k_fp8.view(torch.uint8)
+    flat[blk, BLOCK * HEAD_DIM + off * 4 : BLOCK * HEAD_DIM + off * 4 + 4] = (
+        torch.tensor([scale], dtype=torch.float32).view(torch.uint8)
+    )
+
+
+def cache_read(cache: torch.Tensor, block: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """(fp8 values [16, 128], fp32 scales [16]) of one physical block."""
+    flat = cache.view(cache.shape[0], -1)[block]
+    vals = flat[value_offset(torch.arange(BLOCK)[:, None], torch.arange(HEAD_DIM))]
+    vals = vals.view(FP8)
+    scales = flat[BLOCK * HEAD_DIM : BLOCK * HEAD_DIM + 4 * BLOCK].view(torch.float32)
+    return vals, scales
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------- score / select / CSR
+def paged_logits(iq_fp8, w, cache, block_table, seq_lens, max_len: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[T, max_len] fp32, -inf past seq_len (fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch,
+    next_n == 1)."""
+    T = iq_fp8.shape[0]
+    out = torch.full((T, max_len), float("-inf"))
+    for r in range(T):
+        L = int(seq_lens[r])
+        nb = (L + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
+        vals, scales = zip(
+            *(cache_read(cache, int(block_table[r, b])) for b in range(nb))
+        )
+        K = torch.cat(vals).float()[:L]  # [L, 128]
+        S = torch.cat(scales)[:L]
+        q = iq_fp8[r].float()  # [32, 128]
+        score = torch.relu(K @ q.T) * w[r].float()[None, :]  # [L, 32]
+        out[r, :L] = score.sum(1) * S
+    return out
+
+
+def order_key(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Total order the radix top-k uses (sampler.cu extractBinIdx / isPartialMatch): on
+    the float BITS, so -0.0 ranks below +0.0 and equal values are equal bit patterns.
+    Returned increasing with the value (int64)."""
+    b = x.contiguous().view(torch.int32).long()
+    return torch.where(b >= 0, b ^ (-(2**31)), ~b) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+
+
+def topk_ref(logits: torch.Tensor, seq_lens: torch.Tensor, k: int = TOPK):
+    """-> (canonical indices [T, k] int32, per-row dict(must=set, ties=set, need=int)).
+    Canonical = all values above the k-th value plus the lowest-index threshold ties
+    (the kernel's choice among ties is arrival order)."""
+    T = logits.shape[0]
+    idx = torch.full((T, k), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    info = []
+    for r in range(T):
+        L = int(seq_lens[r])
+        if k >= L:
+            idx[r, :L] = torch.arange(L, dtype=torch.int32)
+            info.append(dict(must=set(range(L)), ties=set(), need=0))
+            continue
+        key = order_key(logits[r, :L])
+        thr = torch.topk(key, k).values[-1]
+        above = torch.nonzero(key > thr).view(-1)
+        ties = torch.nonzero(key == thr).view(-1)
+        need = k - above.numel()
+        sel = torch.cat([above, ties[:need]])
+        idx[r] = sel.to(torch.int32)
+        info.append(dict(must=set(above.tolist()), ties=set(ties.tolist()), need=need))
+    return idx, info
+
+
+def topk_equal_mod_ties(got: torch.Tensor, info: list) -> list[bool]:
+    """Set comparison: every 'must' index present, the rest drawn from the threshold
+    ties, no duplicates."""
+    res = []
+    for r, inf in enumerate(info):
+        g = [int(x) for x in got[r].tolist() if x >= 0]
+        gs = set(g)
+        ok = (
+            len(gs) == len(g)
+            and inf["must"] <= gs
+            and gs - inf["must"] <= inf["ties"]
+            and len(gs - inf["must"]) == inf["need"]
+        )
+        res.append(ok)
+    return res
+
+
+def csr(
+    topk_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    k: int = TOPK,
+):
+    """(indptr [T+1] int32, indices [indptr[-1]] int32) as generate_sparse_seqlen +
+    triton_convert produce them."""
+    T = topk_idx.shape[0]
+    n = torch.clamp(seq_lens.long(), max=k)
+    indptr = torch.zeros(T + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(n, 0).to(torch.int32)
+    out = torch.zeros(int(indptr[-1]), dtype=torch.int32)
+    maxb = block_table.shape[1]
+    for r in range(T):
+        tok = topk_idx[r, : int(n[r])].long()
+        b = torch.div(tok, BLOCK, rounding_mode="floor")
+        valid = (tok >= 0) & (b >= 0) & (b < maxb)
+        base = block_table[r, b.clamp(0, maxb - 1)].long()
+        val = torch.where(valid, base * BLOCK + tok % BLOCK, torch.zeros_like(tok))
+        out[int(indptr[r]) : int(indptr[r + 1])] = val.to(torch.int32)
+    return indptr, out
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ whole decode step
+def decode_step(
+    W: dict,
+    h: torch.Tensor,
+    pos: torch.Tensor,
+    slots: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    cache: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin: torch.Tensor,
+    eps_q: float = 1e-5,
+) -> dict:
+    """W: w_qa [q_lora + ..., H] (only the first q_lora rows used), w_qa_norm [q_lora],
+    w_qb [32*128, q_lora], w_wk [128 + 32, H], k_norm_w / k_norm_b [128]. h: [T, H] bf16
+    (the layer's normed input). ``cache`` is updated in place at ``slots`` (the current
+    tokens) before scoring, as in vLLM."""
+    T = h.shape[0]
+    q_lora = W["w_qa_norm"].shape[0]
+    q_raw = bf16(h.float() @ W["w_qa"][:q_lora].float().T)
+    q_c = bf16(rms_norm(q_raw, W["w_qa_norm"], eps_q))
+    iq = bf16(q_c.float() @ W["w_qb"].float().T).view(T, N_HEAD, HEAD_DIM).float()
+    iq = rope_interleave(iq, cos_sin, pos)
+    iq_fp8, s_q = ue8m0_fp8(iq)  # [T, 32, 128], [T, 32]
+    kw = bf16(h.float() @ W["w_wk"].float().T)
+    w = kw[:, HEAD_DIM:].float() * s_q * (HEAD_DIM**-0.5) * (N_HEAD**-0.5)
+    k = layer_norm(kw[:, :HEAD_DIM], W["k_norm_w"], W["k_norm_b"], 1e-6)
+    k = rope_interleave(k, cos_sin, pos)
+    k_fp8, s_k = ue8m0_fp8(k)
+    for r in range(T):
+        if int(slots[r]) >= 0:
+            cache_write(cache, int(slots[r]), k_fp8[r], float(s_k[r]))
+    logits = paged_logits(iq_fp8, w, cache, block_table, seq_lens, int(seq_lens.max()))
+    top, info = topk_ref(logits, seq_lens)
+    indptr, _ = csr(top, seq_lens, block_table)
+    return dict(
+        iq_fp8=iq_fp8,
+        weights=w,
+        k_fp8=k_fp8,
+        logits=logits,
+        topk=top,
+        topk_info=info,
+        indptr=indptr,
+    )

+"""CPU tests of the indexer_only trim (runtime/indexer_only.py): every value the indexer
+consumes is unchanged, the MQA dummies are persistent zero buffers, and the q-row slice

+class Lin:
+    def __init__(self, rows, noise=0.0, raises=False):
+        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(rows)
+        # small integers: exact sums, so a row-slice GEMM == the full one
+        self.weight = torch.randint(-3, 4, (rows, H), generator=g).float()
+        self.noise, self.raises = noise, raises
+        lin = self
+
+        class QM:
+            def apply(self, layer, x, bias=None):
+                if lin.raises:
+                    raise RuntimeError("needs more than .weight")
+                return x @ layer.weight.T + lin.noise
+
+        self.quant_method = QM()

+    def __call__(self, x):

+        softmax_scale=1.0,

+    )

+        fused_qkv_a_proj=Lin(QL + KVL + PE, noise, raises),
+        q_lora_rank=QL,
+        kv_lora_rank=KVL,

+            ("run", q_c.clone(), iq.clone(), iw.clone())
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def refresh(attn, trim):

+
+
+def run(ref, x):
+    CALLS.clear()
+    ref(torch.arange(x.shape[0]), x)
+    return list(CALLS)

+def test_trim_keeps_indexer_inputs():
+    x = torch.randint(-3, 4, (4, H)).float()
+    attn = make_attn()
+    trimmed = refresh(attn, True)
+    base = run(refresh(attn, False), x)
+    t1 = run(trimmed, x)
+    t2 = run(trimmed, x)
+    # q_c into fused_norm_rope, index_k, index_q and the _run_indexer args are equal
+    assert torch.equal(base[0][1], t1[0][1]) and torch.equal(base[0][2], t1[0][2])
+    assert torch.equal(base[1][5], t1[1][5])
+    assert all(torch.equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(base[2][1:], t1[2][1:]))
+    assert base[0][5] is None and t1[0][5] is None  # the MLA write stays disabled
+    # persistent dummies: the same zero-filled buffers on every call
+    assert t1[1][1] == t2[1][1] and t1[1][2] == t2[1][2] and t1[1][3] and t1[1][4]

+
+def test_trim_falls_back_to_full_gemm():
+    x = torch.randint(-3, 4, (4, H)).float()
+    # the sliced GEMM is not bit-identical -> full GEMM for this row count from now on
+    trimmed = refresh(make_attn(noise=1e-3), True)

+    t = run(trimmed, x)
+    assert trimmed.q_slice_ok == {4: False} and t[0][3] == (4, KVL)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""CPU tests of the golden decode-indexer model (indexer_ref.py) on synthetic data with
+GLM-5.2 shapes (hidden 6144, q_lora 2048, 32 index heads x 128, rope 64 interleaved,
+block 16, top-k 2048), and of the kernel-side address / ordering models built on it."""

+import itertools
+import random

+import torch

+from tests.models.deepseek_v32.amd_specialized_decode import indexer_ref as R

+ITEMS = MAXS // THREADS

+def test_cache_layout():
+    """value_offset == the Triton writer's formula; write/read round trip; scale tail
+    position."""
+    for o in range(16):
+        d = torch.arange(128)
+        # kernels.py:98-103 (TILE 16)
+        triton = o // 16 * 16 * 128 + o % 16 * 16 + d // 16 * 16 * 16 + d % 16
+        assert torch.equal(R.value_offset(o, d), triton)
+    offs = torch.stack([R.value_offset(o, torch.arange(128)) for o in range(16)])
+    # a permutation of the value region
+    assert offs.unique().numel() == 16 * 128 and int(offs.max()) == 2047
+    cache = torch.zeros(5, 16, 132, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    ks = []
+    for slot in (0, 7, 16 * 3 + 15):
+        k = (torch.randn(128, generator=g) * 3).to(R.FP8)
+        R.cache_write(cache, slot, k, 0.125)
+        ks.append((slot, k))
+    for slot, k in ks:
+        v, s = R.cache_read(cache, slot // 16)
+        assert (
+            torch.equal(v[slot % 16].view(torch.uint8), k.view(torch.uint8))
+            and float(s[slot % 16]) == 0.125
+        )
+
+
+def test_ue8m0_and_rope():
+    v = torch.randn(7, 32, 128, generator=g) * torch.logspace(-3, 3, 7)[:, None, None]
+    q, s = R.ue8m0_fp8(v)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.exp2(torch.log2(s).round()), s)  # power of two
+    deq = q.float() * s[..., None]
+    assert (
+        float(q.float().abs().max()) <= 448
+        and float(((deq - v).abs() / v.abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True)).max()) < 0.07
+    )
+    # RoPE: rotation preserves pair norms; pos 0 (cos 1, sin 0) is the identity
+    cs = torch.cat([torch.ones(1, 32), torch.zeros(1, 32)], 1)
+    x = torch.randn(3, 128, generator=g)
+    assert torch.equal(R.rope_interleave(x, cs, torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long)), x)
+    ang = torch.rand(10, 32, generator=g) * 6
+    cs2 = torch.cat([ang.cos(), ang.sin()], 1)
+    y = R.rope_interleave(x, cs2, torch.tensor([3, 4, 9]))
+    n0 = x[:, :64].view(3, 32, 2).norm(dim=-1)
+    n1 = y[:, :64].view(3, 32, 2).norm(dim=-1)
+    assert torch.allclose(n0, n1, atol=1e-5) and torch.equal(y[:, 64:], x[:, 64:])
+
+
+def test_topk_and_csr():
+    # short rows: identity in order, -1 tail
+    logits = torch.randn(3, 6000, generator=g)
+    sl = torch.tensor([5, 2048, 6000])
+    top, info = R.topk_ref(logits, sl)
+    assert (
+        top[0, :5].tolist() == list(range(5))
+        and int(top[0, 5]) == -1
+        and top[1].tolist() == list(range(2048))

+    # is not

+    assert all(R.topk_equal_mod_ties(perm, info))
+    bad = perm.clone()
+    bad[2, 0] = int((set(range(6000)) - set(perm[2].tolist())).pop())

+def test_decode_step_glm_shapes():
+    """Whole step with GLM-5.2 shapes; logits cross-checked by an independent dense
+    recomputation."""
+    H, QL = 6144, 2048
+    T = 3
+    W = dict(
+        w_qa=torch.randn(QL + 576, H, generator=g) / H**0.5,
+        w_qa_norm=1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(QL, generator=g),
+        w_qb=torch.randn(32 * 128, QL, generator=g) / QL**0.5,
+        w_wk=torch.randn(160, H, generator=g) / H**0.5,
+        k_norm_w=1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(128, generator=g),
+        k_norm_b=0.1 * torch.randn(128, generator=g),
+    )
+    seq = torch.tensor([37, 2048, 3100])
+    nblk = 340
+    perm = torch.randperm(nblk, generator=g)
+    bt = torch.zeros(T, 200, dtype=torch.int32)
+    off = 0
+    for r in range(T):
+        nb = (int(seq[r]) + 15) // 16
+        bt[r, :nb] = perm[off : off + nb].int()
+        off += nb
+    cache = torch.zeros(nblk, 16, 132, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    # history keys: random FP8 rows with power-of-2 scales at every position < seq - 1
+    for r in range(T):
+        for p in range(int(seq[r]) - 1):
+            R.cache_write(
+                cache,
+                int(bt[r, p // 16]) * 16 + p % 16,
+                (torch.randn(128, generator=g)).to(R.FP8),
+                2.0 ** int(torch.randint(-6, -2, (1,), generator=g)),
+            )
+    pos = seq - 1
+    slots = torch.tensor(
+        [int(bt[r, int(pos[r]) // 16]) * 16 + int(pos[r]) % 16 for r in range(T)]
+    )
+    ang = torch.outer(
+        torch.arange(4096).float(), 1.0 / (8e6 ** (torch.arange(0, 64, 2).float() / 64))
+    )
+    cos_sin = torch.cat([ang.cos(), ang.sin()], 1)
+    h = torch.randn(T, H, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    out = R.decode_step(W, h, pos, slots, seq, bt, cache, cos_sin)
+    # the current token's index-K is in the cache before scoring and is always selected
+    for r in range(T):
+        v, s = R.cache_read(cache, int(slots[r]) // 16)
+        assert torch.equal(
+            v[int(slots[r]) % 16].view(torch.uint8), out["k_fp8"][r].view(torch.uint8)
+        )
+    # independent dense logits
+    for r in range(T):
+        L = int(seq[r])
+        rows = [R.cache_read(cache, int(bt[r, p // 16])) for p in range(L)]
+        K = torch.stack([rows[p][0][p % 16].float() for p in range(L)])
+        S = torch.stack([rows[p][1][p % 16] for p in range(L)])
+        dense = (
+            torch.relu(torch.einsum("hd,td->th", out["iq_fp8"][r].float(), K))
+            * out["weights"][r]
+        ).sum(1) * S
+        assert torch.allclose(dense, out["logits"][r, :L], rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)
+    assert out["topk"][0, :37].tolist() == list(range(37)) and out["topk"][
+        1
+    ].tolist() == list(range(2048))
+    assert all(R.topk_equal_mod_ties(out["topk"], out["topk_info"]))
+    assert out["indptr"].tolist() == [0, 37, 37 + 2048, 37 + 2 * 2048]
+
+
+def test_fused_kernel_addressing():
+    """The fused indexer's (flydsl/glm/kernel.py) index-cache addressing ==
+    vLLM's SHUFFLE writer (deepseek_v32/common/kernels.py _fp8_quant_and_cache_write,
+    BLOCK_TILE = HEAD_TILE = 16, block 16): cache-stage dword stores (even lane l: dims
+    2l..2l+3), score-stage 8-byte key loads, fp32 scale words."""
+    HD, BS, STRIDE = 128, 16, 16 * 132  # uint8 cache.stride(0)
+
+    def vllm_off(slot, d):  # byte offset of value d of the token at slot
+        return slot // BS * STRIDE + int(R.value_offset(slot % BS, torch.tensor(d)))
+
+    for slot in (0, 5, 15, 16, 37, 16 * 99 + 15):
+        blk, off = slot // 16, slot % 16
+        written = {}
+        # cache stage: byte = blk*stride + off*16 + (i0//16)*256 + i0%16, i0 = 2*lane
+        for lane in range(0, 64, 2):
+            i0 = lane * 2
+            byte = blk * STRIDE + off * 16 + (i0 // 16) * 256 + i0 % 16
+            assert byte % 4 == 0
+            # fp8_pack4(q0, q1, n0, n1): dims i0, i0+1 (own), i0+2, i0+3 (lane+1)
+            for j in range(4):
+                written[i0 + j] = byte + j
+        assert sorted(written) == list(range(HD))
+        assert all(written[d] == vllm_off(slot, d) for d in range(HD))
+        # score stage: k_base = blk*stride + (key%16)*16; k = k32*32 + (lane//16)*8; 8
+        # bytes at k_base+(k//16)*256+k%16
+        k_base = blk * STRIDE + off * 16
+        for k32 in range(HD // 32):
+            for lq in range(4):
+                k = k32 * 32 + lq * 8
+                b0 = k_base + (k // 16) * 256 + k % 16
+                assert b0 % 4 == 0 and [b0 + j for j in range(8)] == [
+                    vllm_off(slot, k + j) for j in range(8)
+                ]
+        # scale: kernel (blk*stride + 16*128 + off*4) // 4 (f32 word) == vLLM
+        # scale_byte_off // 4
+        assert blk * STRIDE + 16 * HD + off * 4 == blk * STRIDE + BS * HD + off * 4
+
+
+def test_ue8m0_exponent_bits():
+    """Kernel _ue8m0_scale (exponent bits + mantissa-nonzero carry) ==
+    2^ceil(log2(fp32(max(amax,1e-4)/448))) exactly, incl. exact powers of two and their
+    neighbours; inverse is the exact reciprocal."""
+    import struct
+
+    def f32(x):
+        return struct.unpack("f", struct.pack("f", x))[0]
+
+    def kernel(amax):
+        # div_rn: correctly rounded fp32 quotient
+        x = f32(max(f32(amax), f32(1e-4)) / 448.0)
+        bits = struct.unpack("I", struct.pack("f", x))[0]
+        e = (bits >> 23) & 255
+        e += 1 if bits & 0x7FFFFF else 0
+        return struct.unpack("f", struct.pack("I", e << 23))[0], struct.unpack(
+            "f", struct.pack("I", (254 - e) << 23)
+        )[0]
+
+    vals = [0.0, 1e-9, 1e-4, 0.0448, 448.0, 448.0 * 2**-10, 1.0, 3.0, 1e4]
+    for k in range(-20, 20):
+        p = 448.0 * 2.0**k
+        vals += [p, f32(p * (1 + 2**-23)), f32(p * (1 - 2**-24))]
+    vals += torch.rand(2000, generator=g).mul(50).exp2().mul(1e-6).tolist()
+    for a in vals:
+        sc, inv = kernel(a)
+        t = torch.tensor([[a, -a]], dtype=torch.float32)
+        ex = float(R.ue8m0_fp8(t, exact=True)[1][0])
+        assert sc == ex, (a, sc, ex)
+        assert sc * inv == 1.0
+        assert f32(a) / sc <= 448.0, a  # in range: no E4M3 overflow
+        lg = float(R.ue8m0_fp8(t)[1][0])  # vLLM-style fp32 log2
+        # only in the fp32-log2 rounding window just above a power of two: 2x, and lg
+        # overflows 448
+        if lg != sc:

+def test_rowpar_layernorm_order():
+    """index_cache_rowpar: LayerNorm statistics as a 64-lane xor-butterfly
+    wave sum of per-lane pairs (k[2l] + k[2l+1]) in fp32, then the kernel's affine /
+    RoPE / ue8m0 FP8 -> vs indexer_ref's golden (torch sums): every difference is a
+    1-code E4M3 neighbour, <= 4 per row (the GPU check's bound), scale
+    identical. (FMA contraction on GPU moves single roundings the same way.)"""
+
+    def wave_sum(v):  # v [rows, 64] fp32, butterfly lane ^ 32, ^ 16, ... ^ 1
+        for off in (32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1):
+            idx = torch.arange(64) ^ off
+            v = v + v[:, idx]
+        return v[:, 0]
+
+    rows = 3000
+    k = (
+        (
+            torch.randn(rows, 128, generator=g)
+            * torch.rand(rows, 1, generator=g).mul(4).exp2()
+        )
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        .float()
+    )
+    gw = 1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(128, generator=g)
+    bw = 0.1 * torch.randn(128, generator=g)
+    cs = (
+        torch.cat(
+            [torch.cos(torch.arange(32.0) * 0.37), torch.sin(torch.arange(32.0) * 0.37)]
+        )
+        .to(torch.bfloat16)
+        .float()[None]
+    )
+    pair = k[:, 0::2] + k[:, 1::2]
+    mean = wave_sum(pair) * (1.0 / 128)
+    d = k - mean[:, None]
+    dd = d[:, 0::2] * d[:, 0::2] + d[:, 1::2] * d[:, 1::2]
+    rstd = torch.rsqrt(wave_sum(dd) * (1.0 / 128) + 1e-6)
+    v = d * rstd[:, None] * gw + bw
+    v = R.rope_interleave(v, cs.expand(1, 64), torch.zeros(rows, dtype=torch.long))
+    kq, ks = R.ue8m0_fp8(v, exact=True)
+    gold = R.rope_interleave(
+        R.layer_norm(k, gw, bw, 1e-6),
+        cs.expand(1, 64),
+        torch.zeros(rows, dtype=torch.long),
+    )
+    gq, gs = R.ue8m0_fp8(gold, exact=True)
+    a, b = kq.view(torch.uint8).int(), gq.view(torch.uint8).int()
+    diff = a != b
+    near = ((a & 0x80) == (b & 0x80)) & (((a & 0x7F) - (b & 0x7F)).abs() == 1)
+    assert bool((near | ~diff).all()), "a non-neighbour FP8 difference"
+    per_row = diff.sum(1)
+    assert int(per_row.max()) <= 4, int(per_row.max())
+    scale_diff = int((ks != gs).sum())
+    assert scale_diff <= rows // 1000

+def test_batched_score_task():
+    """index_score_batched: emulate the batched 64-key score task
+    (flydsl/glm/kernel.py score_task_batched) -- RoPE'd + per-head ue8m0 FP8 index q
+    staged as bf16 pairs, per-lane key words from the SHUFFLE cache, the current key
+    (position L-1) taken from its mailbox words via new_key.select(...) while the cache
+    still holds STALE bytes for that slot (no index_ready wait), C[head, key] of mfma
+    16x16x32 bf16, relu x bf16 head weight x q scale, key scale (mailbox for the current
+    key) x 128^-.5 x 32^-.5 -> == indexer_ref.paged_logits on the cache with the current
+    key written."""
+    HD, NH = 128, 32
+    L, nb_tot = 2100, 200
+    cache = torch.zeros(nb_tot, 16, 132, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    flat = cache.view(nb_tot, -1)
+    flat[:, :2048] = (
+        (torch.randn(nb_tot, 2048, generator=g) * 3).to(R.FP8).view(torch.uint8)
+    )
+    flat[:, 2048:] = (
+        torch.exp2(torch.randint(-8, -2, (nb_tot, 16), generator=g).float())
+        .contiguous()
+        .view(torch.uint8)
+    )
+    bt = torch.randperm(nb_tot, generator=g)[: (L + 15) // 16].int()[None]
+    cur = L - 1
+    slot = int(bt[0, cur // 16]) * 16 + cur % 16
+    # this launch's current key (mailbox values)
+    knew = (torch.randn(HD, generator=g) * 3).to(R.FP8)
+    ksnew = 2.0**-5
+    # what the score task may see: the cache stage has not written the slot yet
+    stale = cache.clone()
+    R.cache_write(cache, slot, knew, ksnew)  # what the golden scores
+    cos_sin = torch.cat(
+        [
+            torch.cos(torch.arange(4096.0)[:, None] * torch.arange(32.0)[None] * 1e-3),
+            torch.sin(torch.arange(4096.0)[:, None] * torch.arange(32.0)[None] * 1e-3),
+        ],
+        1,
+    )
+    cos_sin = cos_sin.to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+    q_raw = (torch.randn(NH, HD, generator=g)).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+    w_raw = torch.randn(NH, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16).float()
+    q = R.rope_interleave(q_raw[None], cos_sin, torch.tensor([cur]))[0]
+    qf, s_q = R.ue8m0_fp8(q, exact=True)
+    w_eff = w_raw * s_q  # keys[h] * keys[32 + h]
+    qb = qf.float().to(torch.bfloat16).float()  # staged bf16 (exact)
+    sflat = stale.view(nb_tot, -1)
+    got = torch.zeros(L)
+    for tile in range((L + 63) // 64):
+        C = torch.zeros(NH, 64)
+        for kg in range(4):
+            for j in range(16):
+                key = tile * 64 + kg * 16 + j
+                safe = min(key, L - 1)
+                blk, off = int(bt[0, safe // 16]), safe % 16
+                vo = R.value_offset(off, torch.arange(HD))
+                kc = sflat[blk, vo].view(R.FP8).float()
+                # new_key.select(mailbox, cache)
+                kv = knew.float() if safe == cur else kc
+                C[:, kg * 16 + j] = qb @ kv
+        part = (torch.relu(C) * w_eff[:, None]).sum(0)
+        for c in range(64):
+            key = tile * 64 + c
+            if key < L:
+                blk, off = int(bt[0, key // 16]), key % 16
+                ksc = (
+                    sflat[blk, 2048 + 4 * off : 2048 + 4 * off + 4]
+                    .contiguous()
+                    .view(torch.float32)[0]
+                )
+                ksc = torch.tensor(ksnew) if key == cur else ksc
+                got[key] = part[c] * ksc * (128**-0.5) * (32**-0.5)
+    ref = R.paged_logits(
+        qf[None],
+        (w_eff * (128**-0.5) * (32**-0.5))[None],
+        cache,
+        bt,
+        torch.tensor([L]),
+        L,
+    )[0]
+    rel = float((got - ref).norm() / ref.norm())
+    assert rel < 1e-6, rel
+    # the stale slot really differs: scoring it from the cache would be wrong
+    assert not torch.equal(stale.view(-1), cache.view(-1))

+def test_select_radix11():
+    """The fused select's 11/11/10-bit radix (descending bins, per-thread
+    bin runs, running count from the top) finds the same threshold key and the same
+    number of threshold ties to take as the exact k-th-largest -> the compaction
+    (unchanged) emits topk_ref's canonical row. Random, heavy ties, -0.0 / +0.0,
+    all-equal and L just above 2048."""
+    K = 2048
+
+    def radix11(keys, k):
+        prefix, remain = 0, k
+        for shift, nbits, hi in ((21, 11, 32), (10, 11, 21), (0, 10, 10)):
+            nb = 1 << nbits
+            hist = [0] * nb
+            for key in keys:
+                if hi == 32 or (key >> hi) == (prefix >> hi):
+                    hist[(key >> shift) & (nb - 1)] += 1
+            run = 0
+            # descending digits = the threads' bin runs in order
+            for d in range(nb - 1, -1, -1):
+                if run < remain <= run + hist[d]:
+                    prefix |= d << shift
+                    remain -= run
+                    break
+                run += hist[d]
+        return prefix, remain  # threshold key, ties to take
+
+    cases = []
+    for L in (2049, 2100, 3000, 4096):
+        cases.append(torch.randn(L, generator=g))
+        cases.append(torch.randint(-3, 4, (L,), generator=g).float())
+        z = torch.where(
+            torch.rand(L, generator=g) < 0.5, torch.tensor(0.0), torch.tensor(-0.0)
+        )
+        z[::5] = torch.randn(len(z[::5]), generator=g)
+        cases.append(z)
+        cases.append(torch.full((L,), 1.5))
+    for x in cases:
+        L = x.numel()
+        keys = R.order_key(x).tolist()
+        thr, rem = radix11(keys, K)
+        srt = sorted(keys, reverse=True)
+        assert thr == srt[K - 1], (L, thr, srt[K - 1])
+        n_gt = sum(k_ > thr for k_ in keys)
+        assert rem == K - n_gt, (L, rem, K - n_gt)
+        # the unchanged compaction: above-threshold ascending, then the lowest-position
+        # `rem` ties
+        above = [i for i, k_ in enumerate(keys) if k_ > thr]
+        ties = [i for i, k_ in enumerate(keys) if k_ == thr]
+        sel = above + ties[:rem]
+        want, _ = R.topk_ref(x[None], torch.tensor([L]))
+        assert sel == want[0].tolist()
+

+def _lds_select(
+    scores: torch.Tensor, barrier_after_digit: bool, order
+) -> tuple[list, list]:
+    """-> (CSR positions written in [0, topk) order, out-of-range offsets written).
+    ``order``: wave order within every barrier phase."""
+    L = scores.numel()
+    key = R.order_key(scores).tolist() + [0] * (MAXS - L)
+    thr_true = sorted(key[:L], reverse=True)[TOPK - 1]
+    # final select_digit's hit thread
+    keys = {256: thr_true, 257: TOPK - sum(k > thr_true for k in key[:L])}
+    wave_state: list[dict] = [dict() for _ in range(WAVES)]
+    out, oob = {}, []
+
+    # phase A (after select_digit's last barrier): every wave reads (prefix, remain) =
+    # keys[256], keys[257]
+    def a_read(w):
+        wave_state[w]["thr"] = keys[256]
+
+    # phase B: item flags + gt scan_flags -> lane 63 of wave w stores keys[256 + w] (its
+    # gt count)
+    def b_write(w):
+        thr = wave_state[w]["thr"]
+        cnt = []
+        for lane in range(LANES):
+            t = w * LANES + lane
+            items = [t * ITEMS + j for j in range(ITEMS)]
+            cnt.append(sum((i < L) and key[i] > thr for i in items))
+        wave_state[w]["cnt"] = cnt
+        keys[256 + w] = sum(cnt)
+
+    # phase C (after scan barrier): offsets from keys[256..263], gt stores
+    def c_store(w):
+        thr = wave_state[w]["thr"]
+        before = sum(keys[256 + v] for v in range(w))
+        run_ = before
+        for lane in range(LANES):
+            t = w * LANES + lane
+            for j in range(ITEMS):
+                i = t * ITEMS + j
+                if i < L and key[i] > thr:
+                    if run_ < TOPK:
+                        out[run_] = i
+                    else:
+                        oob.append(run_)
+                    run_ += 1
+
+    phases = (
+        [[a_read], [b_write], [c_store]]
+        if barrier_after_digit
+        else [[a_read, b_write], [c_store]]
+    )
+    for ph in phases:
+        for w in order:
+            for op in ph:
+                op(w)
+    return [out.get(k, -1) for k in range(TOPK)], oob
+

+def test_barrier_after_select_digit_is_schedule_independent():
+    """CPU model of the fused paged indexer's select-stage LDS protocol
+    (last radix digit through the gt / eq compaction scans): the 8 waves run one at a
+    time between barriers in an adversarial order (a legal GPU interleaving). Without
+    the barrier after select_digit some schedules corrupt the CSR; with it every
+    schedule gives the canonical result."""
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    L = 3500
+    scores = torch.randn(L, generator=g)
+    k = R.order_key(scores)
+    thr = torch.sort(k, descending=True).values[TOPK - 1]
+    want = torch.nonzero(k > thr).view(-1).tolist()  # canonical gt part (ascending)
+    orders = [list(range(WAVES)), list(reversed(range(WAVES)))]
+    rnd = random.Random(1)
+    for _ in range(30):
+        o = list(range(WAVES))
+        rnd.shuffle(o)
+        orders.append(o)
+    # without the barrier: the in-order schedule (lagging waves read after wave 0 / 1
+    # stored their counts) breaks
+    bad = 0
+    for o in orders:
+        got, oob = _lds_select(scores, False, o)
+        if got[: len(want)] != want or oob:
+            bad += 1
+    assert bad > 0, "the model should expose the race without the barrier"
+    # with the barrier: every schedule gives the canonical result
+    for o in orders + [
+        list(p) for p in itertools.islice(itertools.permutations(range(WAVES)), 200)
+    ]:
+        got, oob = _lds_select(scores, True, o)
+        assert got[: len(want)] == want and not oob, o

+def test_poll_xrank_layout():
+    """The flag block is appended after every other symmetric region (no offset
+    moves), one int32 per rank; the target address has an 8-byte scratch slot."""
+    for S, npes in itertools.product((1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12), (1, 2, 4, 8)):
+        scr, sym = layout(S, 8, npes, 2048)
+        old_end = 2 * sym["ffn"]
+        assert sym["poll_xrank"] == old_end and sym["poll_xrank"] % 4 == 0
+        assert all(
+            v <= old_end
+            for k, v in sym.items()
+            if not k.startswith("_") and k != "poll_xrank"
+        )
+        assert sym["_bytes"] >= sym["poll_xrank"] + 4 * npes
+        assert scr["poll_xrank_addr"] % 8 == 0
+        assert scr["_bytes"] >= scr["poll_xrank_addr"] + 8

+def test_poll_watch(monkeypatch):
+    """The executor owns a PollErrorWatch advanced by after_step (from compute_logits);
+    a tripped watch raises; failstop="off" builds none."""
+
+    class FakeWatch:
+        def __init__(self, mono):
+            self.mono, self.n, self.trip = mono, 0, False
+
+        def after_step(self):
+            self.n += 1
+            if self.trip:
+                raise RuntimeError("expired kernel polls -> fail-stop")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(G, "PollErrorWatch", FakeWatch)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", lambda: False)
+    for mode in ("raise", "off"):
+        obj = D.SpecializedDecode.__new__(D.SpecializedDecode)
+        obj.mono, obj.cfg = object(), DecodeConfig(failstop=mode)
+        obj.watch = obj._poll_watch()
+        obj.after_step()
+        if mode == "off":
+            assert obj.watch is None
+            continue
+        assert obj.watch.mono is obj.mono and obj.watch.n == 1
+        obj.watch.trip = True
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="fail-stop"):
+            obj.after_step()

+def test_layer_loop(monkeypatch):

+

+        return lambda p, h, r: _rec(calls, i, (h + 1, h if r is None else r + h))

+    def kernel(i):

+def _quark(attention):
+    """A QuarkConfig like the GLM-5.2 MXFP4 checkpoints: MXFP4 global, attention
+    excluded ("bf16") or given ``attention`` (a weight / input spec pair)."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.quark.quark import QuarkConfig
+
+    mx = dict(
+        dtype="fp4",
+        qscheme="per_group",
+        group_size=32,
+        is_dynamic=False,
+        scale_format="e8m0",
+        ch_axis=-1,
+    )
+    cfg: dict[str, Any] = dict(
+        global_quant_config=dict(weight=mx, input_tensors=dict(mx, is_dynamic=True)),
+        layer_type_quant_config={},
+        layer_quant_config={},
+        exclude=["lm_head"],
+    )
+    names = R.ATTENTION_LINEARS
+    if attention == "bf16":
+        cfg["exclude"] += [  # explicit names, as the checkpoints list them
+            f"model.layers.{L}.self_attn.{p}" for L in range(78) for p in names
+        ]
+    else:
+        w, x = attention
+        cfg["layer_quant_config"] = {
+            f"*self_attn.{p}": dict(weight=w, input_tensors=x, output_tensors=None)
+            for p in names
+        }
+    return QuarkConfig(quant_config=cfg)

+  native K 32 g4 .. + 32 of a 128-K tile, and ONE scale byte; the shared expert's
+  native reader (row-major values, transposed scales) reads the same bytes;
+* the permuted MFMA K order: an emulation of the kernel's A (MXFP4 weights) and B
+  (FP8 activation staged linearly, BF16 mids) operands gives W @ x;
+* the row-major BF16 reader is the old packed tile's operand;
+* weights_from_model on a fake loaded layer: views of the parameters (only w_uk /
+  w_uv copied) and the refusals (fused shared experts, MoE backend, quantized
+  attention, shapes);
+* FP8 checkpoints: the checkpoint's FP8 bytes / per-row scales back from every layout
+  vLLM's FP8 linear kernels leave (aiter preshuffle, hipBLASLt, row-major, [K, N]
+  view) vs a dequantized reference, MLA's BF16 W_UK_T for w_uk, the fused indexer's
+  projections, and the refusals (other FP8 schemes / kernels, FNUZ, scales)."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.flydsl.layout import (
+    atom_mxfp4_scale_index,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.runtime import vllm_weights as VW
+
+E, INTER, HIDDEN = 256, 256, 6144
+FP4 = torch.tensor([0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0.0, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6])
+
+
+def _g(seed=0):
+    return torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+
+
+def _u8(g, *shape):
+    return torch.randint(0, 256, shape, generator=g, dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+
+# aiter's layouts, in pure torch
+def shuffle(x):
+    *_, n, kb = x.shape
+    return (
+        x.reshape(-1, n // 16, 16, kb // 32, 2, 16)
+        .permute(0, 1, 3, 4, 2, 5)
+        .contiguous()
+        .view(x.shape)
+    )
+
+
+def e8m0_shuffle(s):
+    m, n = s.shape
+    return (
+        s.view(m // 32, 2, 16, n // 8, 2, 4)
+        .permute(0, 3, 5, 2, 4, 1)
+        .contiguous()
+        .view(m, n)
+    )
+
+
+# the kernel's reader offsets (glm/kernel.py unit_mxfp4)
+def atom_dword(rg, kc, g4, row, k):
+    return (rg * (k // 64) + kc * 2 + g4 // 2) * 128 + (g4 % 2) * 64 + (row % 16) * 4
+
+
+def native_dword(row, kc, g4, k):
+    return row * (k // 8) + kc * 16 + g4 * 4
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n, k", [(512, 6144), (6144, 256)])
+def test_expert_readers_index_exact(n, k):
+    g = _g(n)
+    nat, s = _u8(g, n, k // 2), _u8(g, n, k // 32)
+    sh, ss, st = (
+        shuffle(nat).view(-1),
+        e8m0_shuffle(s).view(-1),
+        s.t().contiguous().view(-1),
+    )
+    for row in list(range(0, n, n // 64)) + [n - 1]:
+        for kc in range(k // 128):
+            for g4 in range(4):
+                want = nat[row, kc * 64 + g4 * 16 : kc * 64 + g4 * 16 + 16]
+                w = atom_dword(row // 16, kc, g4, row, k)
+                assert torch.equal(sh[4 * w : 4 * w + 16], want)
+                w = native_dword(row, kc, g4, k)
+                assert torch.equal(nat.view(-1)[4 * w : 4 * w + 16], want)
+                col = kc * 4 + g4
+                assert int(ss[atom_mxfp4_scale_index(row, col, k // 32)]) == int(
+                    s[row, col]
+                )
+                assert int(st[col * n + row]) == int(s[row, col])
+
+
+def _fp4(b):
+    return torch.stack([FP4[(b & 15).long()], FP4[(b >> 4).long()]], -1).reshape(-1)
+
+
+def _mfma(a, b):
+    """16x16x32: lane l supplies row / column l % 16, K (l // 16) * 8 .. + 8."""
+    A, B = torch.zeros(16, 32), torch.zeros(32, 16)
+    for ln in range(64):
+        A[ln % 16, (ln // 16) * 8 : (ln // 16) * 8 + 8] = a[ln]
+        B[(ln // 16) * 8 : (ln // 16) * 8 + 8, ln % 16] = b[ln]
+    return A @ B
+
+
+def test_permuted_k_dot():
+    g = _g(1)
+    n, k = 32, 512
+    nat = _u8(g, n, k // 2)
+    s = torch.randint(118, 130, (n, k // 32), generator=g, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    scale = torch.pow(2.0, s.float() - 127).repeat_interleave(32, 1)
+    w = torch.stack([_fp4(nat[r]) for r in range(n)]) * scale
+    x = torch.randn(k, generator=g)
+    sh = shuffle(nat).view(-1)
+    ss = e8m0_shuffle(
+        torch.cat([s, torch.zeros(256 - n, k // 32, dtype=torch.uint8)])
+    ).view(-1)
+    for rg in range(n // 16):
+        c = torch.zeros(16, 16)
+        for kc in range(k // 128):
+            xs = x[kc * 128 : (kc + 1) * 128]
+            for sp in range(4):
+                a, b_bf16, b_fp8 = [], [], []
+                for ln in range(64):
+                    g4, row = ln // 16, rg * 16 + ln % 16
+                    o = atom_dword(rg, kc, g4, row, k)
+                    code = int(ss[atom_mxfp4_scale_index(row, kc * 4 + g4, k // 32)])
+                    a.append(
+                        _fp4(sh[4 * o : 4 * o + 16])[sp * 8 : sp * 8 + 8]
+                        * 2.0 ** (code - 127)
+                    )
+                    bw = g4 * 16 + sp * 4  # BF16 words (2 values)
+                    b_bf16.append(xs[2 * bw : 2 * bw + 8])
+                    fw = g4 * 8 + sp * 2  # linear FP8 words (4 values)
+                    b_fp8.append(xs[4 * fw : 4 * fw + 8])
+                assert all(torch.equal(p, q) for p, q in zip(b_bf16, b_fp8))
+                c += _mfma(a, b_bf16)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            c[:, 0], w[rg * 16 : rg * 16 + 16] @ x, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-4
+        )
+
+
+def _p(x):
+    return torch.nn.Parameter(x, requires_grad=False)
+
+
+def _layer(g, shared_native=True, backend="AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4"):
+    bf = lambda *s: torch.randn(*s, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    m = lambda **kw: NS(**{k: _p(v) for k, v in kw.items()})
+    fp4 = getattr(torch, "float4_e2m1fn_x2", torch.uint8)
+    w13, w2 = _u8(g, E, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN // 2), _u8(g, E, HIDDEN, INTER // 2)
+    # 3-D scales, as vLLM keeps them
+    s13, s2 = _u8(g, E, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN // 32), _u8(g, E, HIDDEN, INTER // 32)
+    gs, ds = (HIDDEN // 32, 2 * INTER), (INTER // 32, HIDDEN)
+    if not shared_native:
+        gs, ds = gs[::-1], ds[::-1]
+    shared = NS(
+        gate_up_proj=m(
+            weight=_u8(g, 2 * INTER, HIDDEN // 2).view(fp4), weight_scale=_u8(g, *gs)
+        ),
+        down_proj=m(
+            weight=_u8(g, HIDDEN, INTER // 2).view(fp4), weight_scale=_u8(g, *ds)
+        ),
+    )
+    experts = NS(
+        w13_weight=_p(w13.view(fp4)),
+        w13_weight_scale=_p(s13),
+        w2_weight=_p(w2.view(fp4)),
+        w2_weight_scale=_p(s2),
+        quant_method=NS(mxfp4_backend=NS(value=backend)),
+    )
+    return NS(
+        input_layernorm=m(weight=bf(HIDDEN)),
+        post_attention_layernorm=m(weight=bf(HIDDEN)),
+        self_attn=NS(
+            q_a_layernorm=m(weight=bf(2048)),
+            kv_a_layernorm=m(weight=bf(512)),
+            fused_qkv_a_proj=m(weight=bf(2624, HIDDEN)),
+            q_b_proj=m(weight=bf(2048, 2048)),
+            o_proj=m(weight=bf(HIDDEN, 2048)),
+            kv_b_proj=m(weight=bf(8 * 448, 512)),
+        ),
+        mlp=NS(
+            gate=NS(
+                weight=_p(bf(E, HIDDEN)),
+                e_score_correction_bias=_p(torch.randn(E, generator=g)),
+            ),
+            experts=NS(routed_experts=experts),
+            shared_experts=shared,
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _params(ns):
+    out = []
+    for v in vars(ns).values():
+        if isinstance(v, torch.nn.Parameter):
+            out.append(v)
+        elif isinstance(v, NS):
+            out += _params(v)
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("native", [True, False])
+def test_weights_from_model_views(native):
+    lay = _layer(_g(2), shared_native=native)
+    t, kw = VW.weights_from_model(lay)
+    assert kw == dict(shared_native=native)
+    storages = {p.untyped_storage().data_ptr() for p in _params(lay)}
+    copies = sorted(
+        k for k, v in t.items() if v.untyped_storage().data_ptr() not in storages
+    )
+    assert copies == ["w_uk", "w_uv"]
+    kv_b = lay.self_attn.kv_b_proj.weight.data.view(8, 448, 512)
+    assert torch.equal(t["w_uk"].view(8, 512, 192), kv_b[:, :192].transpose(1, 2))
+    assert torch.equal(t["w_uv"].view(8, 256, 512), kv_b[:, 192:])
+    assert t["w_ug"].data_ptr() == lay.mlp.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight.data_ptr()
+    assert t["s_ug_sh"].shape == (
+        (HIDDEN // 32, 2 * INTER) if native else (2 * INTER, HIDDEN // 32)
+    )

+def test_weights_from_model_refusals():
+    def refused(lay, what):
+        with pytest.raises(VW.WeightViewError, match=what):
+            VW.weights_from_model(lay)
+
+    g = _g(3)
+    refused(_layer(g, backend="AITER_MXFP4_BF16"), "AITER_MXFP4_BF16")
+    lay = _layer(g)
+    lay.mlp.shared_experts = None
+    refused(lay, "shared")
+    lay = _layer(g)

+        lay.self_attn.o_proj.weight.data.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)

+    lay = _layer(g)
+    ex = lay.mlp.experts.routed_experts

+    refused(lay, "experts.w_dn")
+    lay = _layer(g)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- FP8 checkpoints
+def _fp8(g, *shape):
+    """Random finite E4M3 bytes (0x7F / 0xFF are NaN)."""
+    b = _u8(g, *shape)
+    return torch.where((b & 0x7F) == 0x7F, b ^ 1, b).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def _fp8_linear(g, rows, k, kernel="AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel"):
+    """A Quark PTPC FP8 linear as process_weights_after_loading leaves it under
+    ``kernel``; returns (module, checkpoint values [rows, k], scales [rows])."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
+        kFp8DynamicTokenSym,
+        kFp8StaticChannelSym,
+    )
+
+    q, s = _fp8(g, rows, k), torch.rand(rows, generator=g) * 1e-2 + 1e-4
+    how = VW.FP8_LINEAR_LAYOUTS.get(kernel, "rows")
+    qb = q.view(torch.uint8)
+    if how == "shuffled":
+        w = shuffle(qb).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        w = w.t() if "HipbMM" in kernel else w
+        ws = s.view(1, rows) if "HipbMM" in kernel else s.view(rows, 1)
+    elif "AiterPerToken" in kernel:
+        w, ws = q, s.view(rows, 1)
+    else:
+        w, ws = q.t(), s.view(rows, 1)  # QuarkW8A8Fp8's weight.t() view
+    scheme = type("QuarkW8A8Fp8", (), {})()
+    scheme.weight_quant_key, scheme.activation_quant_key = (
+        kFp8StaticChannelSym,
+        kFp8DynamicTokenSym,
+    )
+    scheme.fp8_linear = type(kernel, (), {})()
+    return NS(weight=_p(w), weight_scale=_p(ws), scheme=scheme), q, s
+
+
+def test_unshuffle_16x16_inverts_aiter_shuffle():

+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kernel", sorted(VW.FP8_LINEAR_LAYOUTS))
+def test_fp8_linear_rows_every_layout(kernel):

+    w, sc = VW.fp8_linear_rows(mod, "x", (2048, 512))

+    assert torch.equal(w.view(torch.uint8), q.view(torch.uint8))

+def _fp8_layer(g, kernel="AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel"):
+    """_layer with the FP8 attention of amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 at TP8."""
+    lay = _layer(g)
+    a, ref = lay.self_attn, {}
+    for name, shape in (
+        ("fused_qkv_a_proj", (2624, HIDDEN)),
+        ("q_b_proj", (2048, 2048)),
+        ("o_proj", (HIDDEN, 2048)),
+        ("kv_b_proj", (8 * 448, 512)),
+    ):
+        mod, q, s = _fp8_linear(g, *shape, kernel)
+        setattr(a, name, mod)
+        ref[name] = (q, s)
+    # MLA's own BF16 dequantization (split_kv_b_proj): W_UK_T [N, P, L]
+    q, s = ref["kv_b_proj"]
+    deq = (q.float() * s[:, None]).to(torch.bfloat16).view(8, 448, 512)
+    a.W_UK_T = _p(deq[:, :192].contiguous())  # (N, P, L) like W_UK.permute(1, 2, 0)
+    return lay, ref
+

+        "s_q_b",

+        "s_uv",
+    ]
+    for key, name in (

+        ("q_b", "q_b_proj"),

+        assert torch.equal(t[f"w_{key}"].view(torch.uint8), q.view(torch.uint8))
+        assert torch.equal(t[f"s_{key}"], s)
+    q, s = ref["kv_b_proj"]
+    assert torch.equal(
+        t["w_uv"].view(torch.uint8).view(8, 256, 512),
+        q.view(torch.uint8).view(8, 448, 512)[:, 192:],
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(t["s_uv"].view(8, 256), s.view(8, 448)[:, 192:])
+    # the dequantized W_UV rows equal the reference dequantization exactly
+    deq = q.float().view(8, 448, 512)[:, 192:] * s.view(8, 448, 1)[:, 192:]
+    assert torch.equal(

+    )
+    assert t["w_uk"].dtype is torch.bfloat16
+    assert torch.equal(
+        t["w_uk"].view(8, 512, 192), lay.self_attn.W_UK_T.data.transpose(1, 2)
+    )

+# GLM-5.2 specialized decode (AMD)
+
+An opt-in decode path for GLM-5.2 on MI355X. It runs each MoE decoder layer
+(layers 3–77) as one persistent FlyDSL kernel inside vLLM's layer loop. Prefill,
+mixed batches and batches above `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` run vLLM's decode unchanged. The
+interface is the `SpecializedDecode` shape of #61867.
+
+## Enabling
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <GLM-5.2 checkpoint> -tp 8 \
+  --additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}' \
+  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
+```
+
+`decode_backend` is `"auto"` (off) by default. If a deployment isn't supported,
+startup fails with one error that lists every reason.
+
+## Supported checkpoints
+
+Attention precision follows the checkpoint. Nothing is re-quantized at load time.
+
+| Checkpoint | Attention | Indexer layers | Validated |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` (MXFP4 experts) | BF16 | vLLM's indexer (`indexer_only`) | GPU: speed, GSM8K |
+| `amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8` (MXFP4 experts, Quark per-channel FP8 attention), `max_model_len` ≤ 4096 | FP8, with the checkpoint's per-row scales | Fused into the kernel | GPU: speed, GSM8K |
+| Same, `max_model_len` > 4096 | FP8, with the checkpoint's per-row scales | vLLM's indexer | CPU tests and compile only |
+
+The fused indexer also needs an FP8 `indexer.wq_b` and a first mono layer that is not
+an indexer layer; otherwise vLLM's indexer runs. The startup log names the path and,
+when the fused indexer is off, why.
+
+Any other attention quantization is refused at startup. That includes block or
+per-tensor FP8, a non-Quark method, and FP8 on only some layers or matrices.
+
+## Supported deployments
+
+- **Hardware:** gfx950 (MI350X / MI355X), TP = 8, Model Runner V2.
+- **Precision:** `dtype=bfloat16`; `kv_cache_dtype` auto or bfloat16.
+- **Graphs:** FULL decode CUDA graphs or eager mode. Any capture sizes and
+  `max_num_seqs` work: captured sizes up to `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` run the kernels, larger
+  ones capture vLLM's decode. PIECEWISE-only graphs run every decode step through
+  vLLM's decode.
+- **Refused at startup:**
+    - PP, DP, EP, DCP, PCP, DBO;
+    - speculative decoding, LoRA, sleep mode, KV-transfer connectors, routed-expert
+    capture;
+    - AITER fused shared experts;
+    - `STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE`;
+    - MRV1.
+- **Checked when the executor is built:** the MoE layout and backend
+  (`AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`), the attention weights and the RoPE table.
+- **Checked at every KV bind:** the caches are bound and contiguous, use the MLA row
+  layout, and are under 4 GiB.
+
+## Batch sizes
+
+Two constants in `runtime/__init__.py` set the limits:
+
+- `BATCH_SIZES = (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)` is every batch size the kernel can be
+  built for.
+- `MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 8` is the largest batch the kernels serve.
+
+A batch pads up to the next built size, so 3 requests run as 4. Above 8 the kernel
+switches to a second row group, and the gain over vLLM falls off quickly (BF16,
+3000-token context, TPOT):
+
+| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| vLLM (ms) | 13.71 | 14.71 | 15.52 | 16.59 | 17.38 | 18.44 | 19.51 |
+| Specialized decode (ms) | 5.94 | 6.81 | 8.46 | 10.13 | 11.55 | 14.84 | 18.41 |
+| Speedup | 2.31× | 2.16× | 1.83× | 1.64× | 1.50× | 1.24× | 1.06× |
+
+FP8-attention checkpoint (`amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, fused indexer), against
+vLLM on the same checkpoint:
+
+| Batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| vLLM (ms) | 14.48 | 15.24 | 15.85 | 16.68 | 17.40 | 18.23 | 19.39 |
+| Specialized decode (ms) | 4.89 | 5.98 | 7.34 | 8.74 | 10.27 | 14.83 | 17.24 |
+| Speedup | 2.96× | 2.55× | 2.16× | 1.91× | 1.69× | 1.23× | 1.12× |
+
+Both variants fall off the same way above 8, so `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` is 8 for both. GSM8K
+(5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions, strict): 1247 BF16; 1230 FP8, against 1226 for vLLM on
+the same FP8 checkpoint.
+
+## Options
+
+These go in `additional_config["specialized_decode"]`. Unknown keys and invalid
+values are refused at startup.
+
+| Key | Default | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `indexer_mode` | `"indexer_only"` | How non-fused indexer layers refresh the top-k: vLLM's indexer alone, or `"attn"` (vLLM's whole attention, slower) |
+| `layers` | 3–77 | Decoder layers that get a kernel |
+| `failstop` | `"raise"` | Expired cross-rank waits: `"raise"` (fail-stop), `"warn"` (log and continue) or `"off"` (no fail-stop watch). With `"warn"` / `"off"` the eager health check still disables the kernels after an expiry |
+| `poll_limit` | 20,000,000 | Bound on each cross-rank wait (about 4 s) |
+| `step_sync`, `check_every` | on in eager mode, off under FULL graphs | Eager-mode health check (a device sync and a CPU all-reduce). `step_sync=True` is refused under FULL graphs; `check_every` has no effect there |
+
+Debug only:
+
+- `debug_no_fused_indexer`;
+- `device_nonfinite`, `failstop_nonfinite`;
+- `enabled`;
+- `poll_early_out`, `indexer_trim`, `cache_hoist`, `split_keys64`.
+
+## Layout
+
+| Path | Holds |
+| --- | --- |
+| `runtime/__init__.py` | `DecodeConfig`, `BATCH_SIZES` / `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `specialized_decode_config()`, `unsupported()` |
+| `runtime/decode.py` | `SpecializedDecode`: `prepare_kv`, `plan`, `Step.layer` (layer mode) |
+| `runtime/mono_layers.py` | Per-layer kernels, step inputs, attention path selection, KV-bind checks |
+| `runtime/vllm_weights.py` | Views of vLLM's loaded weights (BF16, FP8 per-channel, MXFP4 experts) |
+| `runtime/indexer_only.py` | The non-fused indexer refresh |
+| `runtime/guards.py` | Build checks, fail-stop and the poll-error watch (`PollErrorWatch`) |
+| `flydsl/` | The vendored FlyDSL kernel (JIT-compiled) |
+
+The model hooks are in `../model.py` and `../model_state.py`. The tests are in
+`tests/models/deepseek_v32/amd_specialized_decode/`.

+class LayerConfig:
+    """Compile-time geometry of one TP decode shard."""
+
+    name: str
+    hidden: int
+    q_lora: int
+    kv_lora: int
+    pe_dim: int
+    nope_dim: int
+    v_dim: int
+    n_experts: int

+
+    @property
+    def moe_slots(self) -> int:
+        return 1 + self.top_k
+
+    @property
+    def softmax_scale(self) -> float:
+        return (self.nope_dim + self.pe_dim) ** -0.5
+

+GLM5_CONFIG = LayerConfig(
+    name="glm5",
+    hidden=6144,
+    q_lora=2048,
+    kv_lora=512,
+    pe_dim=64,
+    nope_dim=192,
+    v_dim=256,
+    n_experts=256,
+    top_k=8,
+    inter=256,
+    route_scale=2.5,
+    local_heads=8,
+)
+
+GLM5_REFERENCE_TP = 8
+GLM5_TP_SIZES = (4, GLM5_REFERENCE_TP)
+GLM5_KERNEL_SAMPLES = (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2025 FlyDSL Project Contributors
