+# atom/model_ops/monokernel/glm/layout.py). The original source code was licensed under
+# the Apache License 2.0 and included the following copyright notice:
+# Copyright (c) 2025 FlyDSL Project Contributors
+# Modified by the vLLM project contributors (Apache-2.0 sec. 4(b)): import paths
+#   rewritten to this package; POLL_STAGES and the poll_err / poll_abort scratch words,
+#   scratch regions of the in-kernel indexer, a split_keys override of the sparse-MLA
+#   split task size; the DCP region and unused helpers removed.
+
+"""Compile-time storage layout and CTA schedule for the GLM-5 MonoKernel."""
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.flydsl.config import (
+    HIDDEN,
+    INTER,
+    KV_LORA,
+    MOE_SLOTS,
+    N_EXPERTS,
+    NOPE_DIM,
+    PE_DIM,
+    Q_LORA,
+    QKV_A_ROWS,
+    TOP_K,
+    V_DIM,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.flydsl.layout import (
+    BLOCKS,
+    Q_B_TILE,
+    QKV_A_TILE,
+    ROUTER_TILE,
+    ROW_TILE,
+    UG_TILE,
+    UK_TILE,
+    UV_TILE,
+    WAVES,
+)
+
+INDEX_HEADS = 32
+INDEX_DIM = 128
+INDEX_Q_ROWS = INDEX_HEADS * INDEX_DIM
+INDEX_TILE = 16
+INDEX_KEYS_PER_TASK = 64
+
+
+def split_acc_head(head_group, lane_group: int, element: int):
+    """Map one split-PV MFMA row to its local attention head."""
+    return head_group * WAVES + lane_group * 4 + element
+
+
+def split_score_column(wave: int, lane: int):
+    """Locate this wave's head column in a 16x16 MFMA score tile."""
+    return wave + 16 * ((lane % 16) // 4)
+
+
+N_QKV_A = QKV_A_ROWS // QKV_A_TILE
+N_ROW_TILES = HIDDEN // ROW_TILE
+N_ROUTER = N_EXPERTS // ROUTER_TILE
+XQ_BLOCKS = HIDDEN // 128
+XQ_WAVES = (XQ_BLOCKS + N_ROUTER - 1) // N_ROUTER
+assert XQ_WAVES * 4 <= WAVES
+
+
+def dn_tile(samples: int) -> int:
+    """Rows per expert-down / FFN-reduce task."""
+    return 32 if samples == 1 or samples > 4 else HIDDEN // BLOCKS
+
+
+def sparse_keys_per_task(samples: int, heads: int = WAVES) -> int:
+    """Use narrower sparse tiles when samples or attention heads fill LDS."""
+    return 32 if samples > 4 or heads > 2 * WAVES else 64
+
+
+def sample_wave_batches(samples: int) -> int:
+    return (samples + WAVES - 1) // WAVES
+
+
+def ug_task_rounds(inter: int) -> int:
+    return (inter + BLOCKS - 1) // BLOCKS
+
+
+def down_x_words(samples: int, inter: int) -> int:
+    return samples * MOE_SLOTS * inter // 2
+
+
+def ug_split(samples: int, inter: int = INTER):
+    """Return the balanced up/gate leftover split for batches two and four."""
+    full_tiles, remainder = divmod((samples * TOP_K + 1) * (inter // UG_TILE), BLOCKS)
+    if samples not in (2, 4) or remainder == 0 or BLOCKS % remainder:
+        return None
+    segments = BLOCKS // remainder
+    if (HIDDEN // 128) % segments or (HIDDEN // 128) // segments > WAVES // 2:
+        return None
+    return full_tiles, segments
+
+
+# Stages that poll mailboxes, in execution order.  A bounded poll (``poll_limit``,
+# back-ported from FlyDSL #1214's gfx1250 kernel) that expires sets its stage's
+# ``poll_err`` scratch word instead of spinning forever.
+POLL_STAGES = (
+    "qkv_a",
+    "q_norm",
+    "cache",
+    "q_b",
+    "index_q",
+    "uk",
+    "index_score",
+    "index_select",
+    "split",
+    "uv",
+    "o",
+    "router",
+    "ug",
+    "down",
+)
+
+
+def _align(size: int, alignment: int = 256) -> int:
+    return (size + alignment - 1) // alignment * alignment
+
+
+def layout(
+    samples: int,
+    heads: int,
+    npes: int,
+    sparse_attention_topk: int,
+    with_indexer: bool = False,
+    index_max_seq: int = 4096,
+    inter: int = INTER,
+    split_keys: int | None = None,
+):
+    """Return byte offsets for per-rank scratch and symmetric peer buffers.
+    ``split_keys``: keys per sparse-MLA split task (default ``sparse_keys_per_task``; 64
+    with ``split_keys64``).
+    """
+    split_count = sparse_attention_topk // (
+        split_keys or sparse_keys_per_task(samples, heads)
+    )
+    pair_bytes = 8
+    items = [
+        ("q_a", samples * Q_LORA * pair_bytes),
+        ("q_an", samples * Q_LORA // 2 * pair_bytes),
+        ("kv_a", samples * (KV_LORA + PE_DIM) * pair_bytes),
+        ("kvnew", samples * KV_LORA * pair_bytes),
+        ("penew", samples * PE_DIM * pair_bytes),
+        ("q_nope", samples * heads * NOPE_DIM * pair_bytes),
+        ("q_pe", samples * heads * PE_DIM * pair_bytes),
+        ("q_lat", samples * heads * KV_LORA * pair_bytes),
+        ("sp_acc", samples * split_count * heads * KV_LORA * pair_bytes),
+        ("sp_m", samples * split_count * heads * pair_bytes),
+        ("sp_l", samples * split_count * heads * pair_bytes),
+        ("o", samples * heads * V_DIM * pair_bytes),
+        ("a", samples * HIDDEN * pair_bytes),
+        ("scores", samples * N_EXPERTS * pair_bytes),
+        ("xq", samples * HIDDEN // 4 * pair_bytes),
+        ("xqs", samples * XQ_BLOCKS * pair_bytes),
+        ("sel", samples * MOE_SLOTS * pair_bytes),
+        ("prob", samples * MOE_SLOTS * pair_bytes),
+        ("mid", samples * MOE_SLOTS * inter * pair_bytes),
+        ("ugp", BLOCKS * samples * 2 * UG_TILE * pair_bytes),
+        ("xqd", samples * HIDDEN * 4),
+    ]
+    if with_indexer:
+        items += [
+            ("index_k", samples * INDEX_DIM * pair_bytes),
+            ("index_k_new", samples * INDEX_DIM // 2 * pair_bytes),
+            ("index_ready", samples * pair_bytes),
+            ("index_w", samples * INDEX_HEADS * pair_bytes),
+            ("index_q", samples * INDEX_Q_ROWS // 2 * pair_bytes),
+            ("index_scores", samples * index_max_seq * pair_bytes),
+            ("indices", samples * sparse_attention_topk * 4),
+            ("indices_ready", samples * pair_bytes),
+        ]
+    # One word per stage, set by bounded mailbox polls that time out; appended
+    # last so every other offset is unchanged.
+    items.append(("poll_err", 4 * len(POLL_STAGES)))
+    # ``step + 1`` of the step whose first bounded wait expired on this rank (early-out
+    # mark); also appended after everything else so no existing offset moves.
+    items.append(("poll_abort", 4))
+    if with_indexer:
+        # paged fused indexer: this launch's ue8m0 index-K scale per sample (the
+        # unscaled FP8 values go through index_k_new); appended last, no other offset
+        # moves
+        items.append(("index_k_scale", samples * pair_bytes))
+
+    # address of this rank's poll_xrank word on rank 0, written once by the host
+    items.append(("poll_xrank_addr", 8))
+
+    offset, scratch = 0, {}
+    for name, size in items:
+        scratch[name] = offset
+        offset += _align(size)
+    scratch["_bytes"] = offset
+
+    part = npes * samples * HIDDEN * pair_bytes
+    region = 2 * part
+    symmetric = {
+        "attn": 0,
+        "ffn": region,

+def fp8_attention_of(t: dict) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+    """The attention matrices given as FP8 (those with an ``s_<name>`` row scale)."""
+    return tuple(name for name in FP8_ATTENTION if f"s_{name}" in t)

+    """``pack_fp8`` tiles of FP8 [rows, K] ``w_<name>`` + its F32 [rows] scales."""
+    w, s = t[f"w_{name}"], t[f"s_{name}"]

+    x: torch.Tensor, name: str, shape: tuple[int, ...], dtype=None

+    faulting, so every tensor it reads in place must have exactly the expected shape /
+    element size and be contiguous.
+    """
+    ok = (

+        and x.is_contiguous()

+def prepare_glm5_weights(W: LayerWeights) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:

+    aiter's (16, 16) shuffle + e8m0_shuffle scales, the shared expert's own tensors);
+    a checkpoint's FP8 attention matrices (``s_<name>`` given) packed into 16 x 64
+    tiles (a layout copy: the values and scales are the checkpoint's).
+    """
+    t, cfg = W.t, W.config
+    bf, hidden, inter, E = torch.bfloat16, HIDDEN, cfg.inter, N_EXPERTS
+    names = (
+        "w_qkv_a",
+        "w_q_b",
+        "w_uk",
+        "w_uv",
+        "w_o",
+        "w_r",
+        "w_ug",
+        "s_ug",
+        "w_dn",
+        "s_dn",
+        "w_ug_sh",
+        "s_ug_sh",
+        "w_dn_sh",
+        "s_dn_sh",

+        ("s_ug", (E * 2 * inter, hidden // 32)),
+        ("w_dn", (E, hidden, inter // 2)),
+        ("s_dn", (E * hidden, inter // 32)),

+            or index_cache.dim() != 3

+                f"{tuple(index_cache.shape)} {index_cache.dtype}"

+            or index_cache.stride(1) != INDEX_DIM + 4
+            or index_cache.stride(0) % 4

+            [
+                index_cache.data_ptr(),
+                block_table.data_ptr(),
+                block_table.stride(0),
+                index_cache.stride(0),
+            ],
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+        )
+        self.index_params[8:12].copy_(vals)
+        # keep the pointed-to storage alive
+        self._index_tables = (index_cache, block_table)
+

+        self.step.add_(1)

+"""Small ctypes wrapper for the HIP IPC memory operations of the peer buffer."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ctypes
+import os
+
+HIP_IPC_HANDLE_BYTES = 64
+HIP_IPC_MEM_LAZY_ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS = 0x1
+_RANGE_START_ADDR = 11
+
+
+class _HipIpcMemHandle(ctypes.Structure):
+    _fields_ = [("reserved", ctypes.c_byte * HIP_IPC_HANDLE_BYTES)]
+
+
+class HipRuntime:
+    """Load HIP once and expose the host operations used by peer-memory wrappers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, library=None) -> None:
+        self._library = library
+        self._configured_library = None
+
+    def library(self):
+        """Return the configured HIP ctypes library, loading it on first use."""
+        if self._library is None:
+            sonames = (
+                "libamdhip64.so",
+                "libamdhip64.so.7",
+                "libamdhip64.so.6",
+                "libamdhip64.so.5",
+            )
+            candidates = []
+            rocm_path = os.environ.get("ROCM_PATH")
+            if rocm_path:
+                candidates.extend(
+                    os.path.join(rocm_path, lib_dir, name)
+                    for lib_dir in ("lib", "lib64")
+                    for name in sonames
+                )
+            candidates.extend(sonames)
+            for name in candidates:
+                try:
+                    self._library = ctypes.CDLL(name)
+                    break
+                except OSError:
+                    continue
+            if self._library is None:
+                raise RuntimeError("Failed to load HIP runtime library")
+        self._configure(self._library)
+        return self._library
+
+    def _configure(self, library) -> None:
+        if self._configured_library is library:
+            return
+        library.hipIpcGetMemHandle.restype = ctypes.c_int
+        library.hipIpcGetMemHandle.argtypes = [
+            ctypes.POINTER(_HipIpcMemHandle),
+            ctypes.c_void_p,
+        ]
+        library.hipIpcOpenMemHandle.restype = ctypes.c_int
+        library.hipIpcOpenMemHandle.argtypes = [
+            ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_void_p),
+            _HipIpcMemHandle,
+            ctypes.c_uint,
+        ]
+        library.hipIpcCloseMemHandle.restype = ctypes.c_int
+        library.hipIpcCloseMemHandle.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
+        library.hipGetErrorString.restype = ctypes.c_char_p
+        library.hipGetErrorString.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int]
+        library.hipPointerGetAttribute.restype = ctypes.c_int
+        library.hipPointerGetAttribute.argtypes = [
+            ctypes.c_void_p,
+            ctypes.c_int,
+            ctypes.c_void_p,
+        ]
+        self._configured_library = library
+
+    def check(self, error: int, *, operation: str) -> None:
+        """Raise a descriptive exception when a HIP call fails."""
+        if int(error) == 0:
+            return
+        try:
+            value = self.library().hipGetErrorString(int(error))
+            message = (
+                value.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+                if value
+                else f"hipError({error})"
+            )
+        except Exception:
+            message = f"hipError({error})"
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{operation} failed: {message}")
+
+    def get_allocation_base(self, device_pointer: int) -> int:
+        """Return the hipMalloc allocation base containing ``device_pointer``."""
+        base = ctypes.c_void_p()
+        error = self.library().hipPointerGetAttribute(
+            ctypes.byref(base),
+            ctypes.c_int(_RANGE_START_ADDR),
+            ctypes.c_void_p(int(device_pointer)),
+        )
+        self.check(error, operation="hipPointerGetAttribute(RANGE_START_ADDR)")
+        if base.value is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "hipPointerGetAttribute(RANGE_START_ADDR) returned a null "
+                "allocation base"
+            )
+        return int(base.value)
+
+    def get_ipc_handle(self, allocation_base: int) -> bytes:
+        """Export a fixed-size HIP IPC handle for an allocation base pointer."""
+        handle = _HipIpcMemHandle()
+        error = self.library().hipIpcGetMemHandle(
+            ctypes.byref(handle), ctypes.c_void_p(int(allocation_base))
+        )
+        self.check(error, operation="hipIpcGetMemHandle")
+        return bytes(ctypes.string_at(ctypes.byref(handle), HIP_IPC_HANDLE_BYTES))
+
+    def open_ipc_handle(self, handle_bytes: bytes) -> int:
+        """Map a peer allocation and return its local base pointer."""
+        if len(handle_bytes) != HIP_IPC_HANDLE_BYTES:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"expected a {HIP_IPC_HANDLE_BYTES}-byte HIP IPC handle, "
+                f"got {len(handle_bytes)} bytes"
+            )
+        handle = _HipIpcMemHandle()
+        ctypes.memmove(ctypes.byref(handle), bytes(handle_bytes), HIP_IPC_HANDLE_BYTES)
+        mapped_base = ctypes.c_void_p()
+        error = self.library().hipIpcOpenMemHandle(
+            ctypes.byref(mapped_base),
+            handle,
+            ctypes.c_uint(HIP_IPC_MEM_LAZY_ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS),
+        )
+        self.check(error, operation="hipIpcOpenMemHandle")
+        if mapped_base.value is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("hipIpcOpenMemHandle returned a null mapped pointer")
+        return int(mapped_base.value)
+
+    def close_ipc_handle(self, mapped_base: int) -> None:
+        """Close a peer mapping returned by :meth:`open_ipc_handle`."""
+        error = self.library().hipIpcCloseMemHandle(ctypes.c_void_p(int(mapped_base)))
+        self.check(error, operation="hipIpcCloseMemHandle")
+
+
+_DEFAULT_RUNTIME = HipRuntime()
+
+
+def get_allocation_base(device_pointer: int) -> int:
+    """Return the base of the HIP allocation containing ``device_pointer``."""
+    return _DEFAULT_RUNTIME.get_allocation_base(device_pointer)
+
+
+def get_ipc_handle(allocation_base: int) -> bytes:
+    """Export an IPC handle for ``allocation_base``."""
+    return _DEFAULT_RUNTIME.get_ipc_handle(allocation_base)
+
+
+def open_ipc_handle(handle_bytes: bytes) -> int:
+    """Open a peer IPC handle and return its mapped base pointer."""
+    return _DEFAULT_RUNTIME.open_ipc_handle(handle_bytes)
+
+
+def close_ipc_handle(mapped_base: int) -> None:
+    """Close a peer mapping returned by :func:`open_ipc_handle`."""
+    _DEFAULT_RUNTIME.close_ipc_handle(mapped_base)
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "close_ipc_handle",
+    "get_allocation_base",
+    "get_ipc_handle",
+    "open_ipc_handle",
+]

+"""Host-side weight packing for the MonoKernel launch wrapper."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+
+
+def pack_fp8(q: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pack FP8 ``[..., N, K]`` for the kernel's 16-row, 64-K MFMA tiles."""
+    *lead, rows, k = q.shape
+    if rows % 16 or k % 64:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"FP8 matrix dimensions must be divisible by (16, 64), got {(rows, k)}"
+        )
+    w8 = q.view(torch.uint8).reshape(*lead, rows // 16, 16, k // 64, 2, 4, 8)
+    nlead = len(lead)
+    order = list(range(nlead)) + [nlead + position for position in (0, 2, 4, 1, 3, 5)]
+    return w8.permute(*order).contiguous().view(-1)

+                mine = (get_ipc_handle(base), self.local_address - base)
+            except Exception as error:
+                local_error = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+
+            readiness = [None] * npes
+            dist.all_gather_object(readiness, (local_error, mine), group=group)
+            failed = [
+                (peer, status[0])
+                for peer, status in enumerate(readiness)
+                if status[0] is not None
+            ]
+            if failed:
+                detail = "; ".join(f"rank {peer}: {error}" for peer, error in failed)
+                raise RuntimeError(f"symmetric peer allocation/export failed: {detail}")
+
+            addresses = []
+            open_error = None
+            for peer_rank, (_, peer) in enumerate(readiness):
+                handle, offset = peer
+                if peer_rank == rank:
+                    addresses.append(self.local_address)
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    remote_base = open_ipc_handle(handle)
+                    self._remote_bases.append(remote_base)
+                    addresses.append(remote_base + offset)
+                except Exception as error:
+                    open_error = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
+                    break
+
+            open_status = [None] * npes
+            dist.all_gather_object(open_status, open_error, group=group)
+            failed = [
+                (peer, error)
+                for peer, error in enumerate(open_status)
+                if error is not None
+            ]
+            if failed:
+                for remote_base in self._remote_bases:
+                    with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
+                        close_ipc_handle(remote_base)
+                self._remote_bases.clear()
+                detail = "; ".join(f"rank {peer}: {error}" for peer, error in failed)
+                raise RuntimeError(f"symmetric peer open failed: {detail}")
+
+            dist.barrier(group=group)
+        assert device is not None
+        self.addresses = torch.tensor(addresses, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.2 specialized decode: one FlyDSL MonoKernel per MoE decoder layer inside the
+stock layer loop (layer mode), enabled by
+``additional_config={"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}``. Options (the
+``DecodeConfig`` fields) go under ``additional_config["specialized_decode"]``.
+
+``specialized_decode_config`` runs in the model's ``__init__``, before the weights
+load. It returns None for the stock decode, and raises with every reason from
+``unsupported`` when the specialized decode is requested for a deployment it cannot
+serve. Checks that need the loaded weights run when the executor is built
+(``decode.SpecializedDecode``), those that need the KV cache in ``prepare_kv``."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.flydsl.config import (
+    GLM5_KERNEL_SAMPLES,
+)
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+AUTO, SPECIALIZED = "auto", "latency_specialized"
+# additional_config key of the DecodeConfig options
+OPTIONS = "specialized_decode"
+# batch sizes the GLM kernel can be built for (at most 12 requests per step at TP8)
+BATCH_SIZES = GLM5_KERNEL_SAMPLES
+# largest decode batch the kernels serve; larger batches run vLLM's decode. Above 8
+# the kernel switches to a second row group: TPOT vs vLLM is 1.50x at batch 8, 1.24x
+# at 10 and 1.06x at 12, and throughput peaks at 8 (MI355X, BF16, 3k context)
+MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 8
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DecodeConfig:
+    """Step and kernel options. ``decode_config`` fills it from the defaults, the
+    ``additional_config["specialized_decode"]`` options and vLLM's max_model_len."""
+
+    layers: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(3, 78))
+    poll_limit: int = 20_000_000  # ~4 s per mailbox wait
+    # indexer layers refresh the top-k through vLLM's attention ("attn") or the
+    # indexer alone ("indexer_only")
+    indexer_mode: str = "indexer_only"
+    # eager only: rank-uniform state vote (device sync + CPU all-reduce)
+    step_sync: bool = True
+    check_every: int = 1  # eager health check every N kernel steps (0 = never)
+    max_model_len: int = 4096  # RoPE table rows
+    enabled: bool = True  # initial state
+    poll_early_out: bool = True  # after one expired poll, skip the step's other waits
+    indexer_trim: bool = True  # indexer_only: skip work whose results are discarded
+    cache_hoist: bool = True  # cache stage: positions / slots loaded ahead of its wait
+    split_keys64: bool = True  # 64-key sparse-MLA split tasks (batch sizes <= 8 only)
+    # debug: FP8-attention checkpoints run the non-fused indexer path (A/B checks)
+    debug_no_fused_indexer: bool = False
+    # captured isfinite count of each step's output (+ fail-stop on it)
+    device_nonfinite: bool = False
+    failstop_nonfinite: bool = False
+    # expired kernel polls: "raise" (fail-stop), "warn" (log and continue) or "off" (no
+    # fail-stop watch); with "warn" / "off" the eager health check (check_every) still
+    # disables the kernels after an expiry
+    failstop: str = "raise"
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        for name, allowed in (
+            ("indexer_mode", ("attn", "indexer_only")),
+            ("failstop", ("raise", "warn", "off")),
+        ):
+            if getattr(self, name) not in allowed:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be one of {allowed}")
+
+    @property
+    def batch_sizes(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        """The batch sizes the kernels are built for; a smaller batch pads up to the
+        next one."""
+        return tuple(b for b in BATCH_SIZES if b <= MAX_BATCH_SIZE)
+
+
+def decode_backend(vllm_config) -> str:
+    """The requested decode backend: the one place that reads the switch."""
+    extra = vllm_config.additional_config
+    return extra.get("decode_backend", AUTO) if isinstance(extra, dict) else AUTO
+
+
+def specialized_decode_config(vllm_config) -> DecodeConfig | None:
+    """The deployment's specialized decode settings, None for the stock decode.
+    Raises when the specialized decode is requested for an unsupported deployment,
+    listing every reason."""
+    backend = decode_backend(vllm_config)
+    if backend == AUTO:
+        return None
+    if backend != SPECIALIZED:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"decode_backend must be '{AUTO}' or '{SPECIALIZED}', got {backend!r}"
+        )
+    reasons, cfg = _reasons_and_config(vllm_config)
+    if reasons:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "GLM-5.2 specialized decode (decode_backend=latency_specialized) does not "
+            "support: " + "; ".join(reasons) + f" (decode_backend={AUTO} runs vLLM's "
+            "decode)"
+        )
+    if piecewise_graphs_only(vllm_config):
+        logger.warning(
+            "GLM-5.2 specialized decode: PIECEWISE-only breakable cudagraphs capture "
+            "every decode step as stock; use FULL decode graphs or eager mode"
+        )
+    assert cfg is not None
+    return cfg
+
+
+def decode_config(vllm_config) -> DecodeConfig:
+    """The defaults, overridden by ``additional_config["specialized_decode"]``. The
+    RoPE table covers vLLM's max_model_len; step_sync (a device sync and a CPU
+    all-reduce per step) defaults off under FULL graphs."""
+    over = dict(vllm_config.additional_config.get(OPTIONS) or {})
+    if "layers" in over:
+        over["layers"] = tuple(over["layers"])
+    over.setdefault("step_sync", not full_cudagraphs(vllm_config))
+    mml = int(vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len)
+    if over.setdefault("max_model_len", mml) < mml:
+        logger.warning(
+            "GLM-5.2 specialized decode: raising the RoPE table length %d -> vLLM "
+            "max_model_len %d",
+            over["max_model_len"],
+            mml,
+        )
+        over["max_model_len"] = mml
+    return DecodeConfig(**over)
+
+
+def unsupported(vllm_config) -> list[str]:
+    """Every reason this deployment cannot run the specialized decode (empty: it
+    can). Config only: the loaded weights are checked when the executor is built."""
+    return _reasons_and_config(vllm_config)[0]
+
+
+def _reasons_and_config(vllm_config) -> tuple[list[str], DecodeConfig | None]:
+    """``unsupported``'s reasons and the ``DecodeConfig`` (None if the options are
+    invalid), so that ``decode_config`` runs once."""
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.config import CompilationMode
+
+    mc, pc = vllm_config.model_config, vllm_config.parallel_config
+    model_type = getattr(mc.hf_config, "model_type", None)
+    kv_dtype = vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype
+    checks = (
+        (model_type != "glm_moe_dsa", f"model_type {model_type} (GLM-5.2 only)"),
+        (pc.tensor_parallel_size != 8, f"TP {pc.tensor_parallel_size} (TP8 only)"),
+        (pc.pipeline_parallel_size != 1, "pipeline parallelism"),
+        (pc.data_parallel_size != 1, "data parallelism"),
+        (pc.enable_expert_parallel, "expert parallelism"),
+        (pc.decode_context_parallel_size != 1, "decode context parallelism"),
+        (pc.prefill_context_parallel_size != 1, "prefill context parallelism"),
+        # the kernels read one batch's attention metadata per step
+        (pc.use_ubatching, "DBO (dual-batch overlap)"),
+        (vllm_config.speculative_config is not None, "speculative decoding"),
+        # the kernels read the loaded weights in place; a wake-up reloads them
+        (mc.enable_sleep_mode, "sleep mode"),
+        # the kernels replace vLLM's linear and attention layers
+        (vllm_config.lora_config is not None, "LoRA"),
+        (vllm_config.kv_transfer_config is not None, "KV transfer connectors"),
+        (
+            vllm_config.aux_output_config.enable_return_routed_experts,
+            "routed-expert capture",
+        ),
+        # the kernels read the routed and shared experts' own tensors
+        (
+            bool(rocm_aiter_ops.is_fusion_moe_shared_experts_enabled()),
+            "fused shared experts (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1)",
+        ),
+        (mc.dtype != torch.bfloat16, f"dtype {mc.dtype} (bfloat16 only)"),
+        (
+            kv_dtype not in ("auto", "bfloat16"),
+            f"kv_cache_dtype {kv_dtype} (bfloat16 only)",
+        ),
+        # the model state hooks build the executor and bind it to each KV cache
+        (
+            not vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner,
+            "the V1 model runner (set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1)",
+        ),
+        # plan() and the per-layer kernels run in forward; a compiled forward would
+        # trace them (DeepseekV32Model has no @support_torch_compile)
+        (
+            vllm_config.compilation_config.mode == CompilationMode.STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE,
+            "torch.compile (compilation mode STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE)",
+        ),
+    )
+    reasons = [why for bad, why in checks if bad]
+    why = _platform_reason()
+    if why is not None:
+        reasons.append(why)
+    try:
+        cfg = decode_config(vllm_config)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
+        return reasons + [f'additional_config["{OPTIONS}"]: {e}'], None
+    reasons += attention_quant_reasons(vllm_config, cfg.layers)
+    if cfg.step_sync and full_cudagraphs(vllm_config):
+        reasons.append(
+            "step_sync=True under FULL cudagraphs (its device sync and CPU all-reduce "
+            "cannot run inside a graph capture)"
+        )
+    return reasons, cfg
+
+
+# the attention linears as the checkpoint names them (fused_qkv_a_proj = q_a | kv_a)
+ATTENTION_LINEARS = (
+    "q_a_proj",
+    "kv_a_proj_with_mqa",
+    "q_b_proj",
+    "kv_b_proj",
+    "o_proj",
+    "indexer.wq_b",
+)
+
+
+def attention_quant_reasons(vllm_config, layers) -> list[str]:
+    """Why the mono layers' attention linears cannot be read as checkpointed: each must
+    be BF16 (excluded from quantization) or Quark per-channel FP8 with per-token
+    dynamic activations (PTPC), which the kernel reads with its per-row scales, and the
+    attention proper (all but ``indexer.wq_b``) one precision on every mono layer.
+    Block / per-tensor FP8 and non-Quark quantization (e.g. zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8) are
+    refused: the specialized decode never requantizes weights."""
+    qc = getattr(vllm_config, "quant_config", None)
+    if qc is None:
+        return []
+    if qc.get_name() != "quark":
+        name = qc.get_name()
+        return [f"quantization {name} (Quark with BF16 or per-channel FP8 attention)"]
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import LinearBase, UnquantizedLinearMethod
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
+        kFp8DynamicTokenSym,
+        kFp8StaticChannelSym,
+    )
+
+    bad: dict[str, set[int]] = {}
+    # (layer, linear) -> FP8 of the attention proper's linears
+    fp8: dict[int, dict[str, bool]] = {}
+    for L in layers:
+        for proj in ATTENTION_LINEARS:
+            prefix = f"model.layers.{L}.self_attn.{proj}"
+            try:
+                wk, ak, method = qc.get_quant_method_target(prefix, LinearBase)
+            except (NotImplementedError, ValueError) as e:
+                why = f"{proj}: {e}"
+            else:
+                is_bf16 = method is UnquantizedLinearMethod
+                if is_bf16 or (
+                    wk == kFp8StaticChannelSym and ak == kFp8DynamicTokenSym
+                ):
+                    if proj != "indexer.wq_b":
+                        fp8.setdefault(L, {})[proj] = not is_bf16
+                    continue
+                why = f"{proj} quantized as {wk} / {ak}"
+            bad.setdefault(why, set()).add(L)
+    reasons = [
+        f"{why} on layers {sorted(Ls)[0]}..{sorted(Ls)[-1]} (attention must be BF16 or "
+        "per-channel FP8 with per-token activations)"
+        for why, Ls in bad.items()
+    ]
+    partial = sorted(L for L, d in fp8.items() if len(set(d.values())) > 1)
+    if partial:
+        d = fp8[partial[0]]
+        reasons.append(
+            f"partial FP8 attention on layers {partial[0]}..{partial[-1]} (layer "
+            f"{partial[0]}: FP8 {[p for p, v in d.items() if v]}, BF16 "
+            f"{[p for p, v in d.items() if not v]}; a layer's attention is read all "
+            "BF16 or all FP8)"
+        )
+    elif len({next(iter(d.values())) for d in fp8.values() if d}) > 1:
+        on = sorted(L for L, d in fp8.items() if any(d.values()))
+        reasons.append(
+            f"mixed attention precision across mono layers (FP8 on {len(on)} layers, "
+            f"{on[0]}..{on[-1]}; BF16 on the others)"
+        )
+    return reasons
+
+
+def _platform_reason() -> str | None:
+    try:
+        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx950
+
+        return None if on_gfx950() else "this GPU (gfx950 / MI350X only)"
+    except Exception as e:
+        return f"this platform (gfx950 check failed: {e!r})"
+
+
+def full_cudagraphs(vc) -> bool:
+    """FULL (whole-forward) cudagraphs: replays run no Python, so the step decision
+    and every flag it reads are baked in at capture."""
+    mode = vc.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode
+    return mode is not None and bool(mode.has_full_cudagraphs())
+
+
+def piecewise_graphs_only(vc) -> bool:
+    """Decode steps captured as breakable PIECEWISE graphs only: plan() runs them
+    stock."""
+    mode = vc.compilation_config.cudagraph_mode
+    if mode is None or full_cudagraphs(vc) or mode.name == "NONE":
+        return False
+    from vllm import envs as vllm_envs
+
+    return bool(vllm_envs.VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The GLM-5.2 specialized decode executor (layer mode): one routing decision per step,
+then a MonoKernel per MoE decoder layer inside the stock layer loop.
+
+Built by the model state once the weights are loaded (``DeepseekV32ModelState``): reads
+vLLM's loaded weights in place (``vllm_weights``), builds the kernels of every batch
+size, the buffers and the IPC peers, before memory profiling and graph capture.
+``prepare_kv`` binds it to every KV cache vLLM allocates (the CUDA-graph
+memory-profiling cache, then the real one). Each step ``plan`` returns a ``Step`` or
+None; ``Step.layer(i)`` is the kernel callable of mono layer i (None for vLLM's layers
+0..2). Weight reloads are not supported."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from functools import partial
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import CUDAGraphMode
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context, is_forward_context_available
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.runtime import (
+    DecodeConfig,
+    guards,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.runtime.mono_layers import (
+    MonoLayers,
+    mla_cache,
+)
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# (positions, hidden_states, residual) -> (hidden_states, residual)
+LayerKernel = Callable[
+    [torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
+]
+
+
+class Step(NamedTuple):
+    """A planned step: a batch of T rows padded to the built batch size S."""
+
+    T: int
+    S: int
+    kernels: dict[int, LayerKernel]
+
+    def layer(self, idx: int) -> LayerKernel | None:
+        """The kernel replacing decoder layer idx in this step, or None (vLLM's)."""
+        return self.kernels.get(idx)
+
+
+def moe_refusal(backbone, cfg: DecodeConfig) -> str | None:
+    """None if every mono layer's MoE weights have the layout the kernel reads in
+    place (``vllm_weights.unsupported_moe``), else why not."""
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.runtime.vllm_weights import (
+        unsupported_moe,
+    )
+
+    for L in cfg.layers:
+        why = unsupported_moe(backbone.layers[L].mlp)
+        if why is not None:
+            return f"layer {L}: {why}"
+    return None
+
+
+class SpecializedDecode:
+    """The executor: builds the mono layers, binds them to each KV cache and plans
+    every step (layer mode)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, backbone, cfg: DecodeConfig):
+        why = moe_refusal(backbone, cfg)
+        if why is not None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "GLM-5.2 specialized decode does not support the loaded weights: "
+                f"{why} (decode_backend=auto runs vLLM's decode)"
+            )
+        guards.check_rope_table(backbone, cfg)
+        self.backbone, self.cfg = backbone, cfg
+        self.mono = MonoLayers(backbone, cfg)
+        self.kernels: dict[int, LayerKernel] = {
+            L: partial(self.mono.run_layer, layer)
+            for L, layer in self.mono.layers.items()
+        }
+        # (data_ptr, numel) of the first mono layer's KV cache prepare_kv bound
+        self._kv: tuple[int, int] | None = None
+        self.watch = self._poll_watch()
+        logger.info(
+            "GLM-5.2 specialized decode: layers %d..%d, batch sizes %s; larger batches "
+            "run vLLM's decode",
+            self.mono.first,
+            self.mono.last,
+            self.mono.batch_sizes,
+        )
+
+    def _poll_watch(self):
+        """Fail-stop on expired kernel polls, advanced by ``after_step``;
+        ``failstop="off"`` disables it, ``"warn"`` logs."""
+        if self.cfg.failstop == "off":
+            logger.warning("failstop=off: no poll-error fail-stop watch")
+            return None
+        return guards.PollErrorWatch(self.mono)
+
+    def prepare_kv(self) -> None:
+        """Bind the kernels to the KV caches vLLM just bound (the CUDA-graph memory
+        profiling cache, then the real one), checking them (``bind_caches``)."""
+        self._kv = None
+        kv = mla_cache(self.mono.layers[self.mono.first])
+        if kv is None or kv.numel() == 0:
+            return
+        self.mono.bind_caches()
+        self._kv = (kv.data_ptr(), kv.numel())
+
+    def plan(self, positions: torch.Tensor, intermediate_tensors) -> Step | None:
+        """This step's plan, or None to run vLLM's layers.
+
+        Steps that run vLLM's layers:
+        - pipeline-parallel stage inputs, and steps before a KV cache is bound
+          (profiling, dummy runs);
+        - PIECEWISE steps (captured without attention metadata);
+        - steps with prefill rows, batches larger than MAX_BATCH_SIZE or top-k other
+          than 2048 (``mono_layers.step_reason``) and, eager, a rank-uniform no-go vote.
+
+        Eager steps (enforce_eager, or batch sizes FULL graphs did not capture) run
+        the kernels too. Every predicate is the same on all TP ranks: the kernels'
+        mailboxes need every rank on one path. Under FULL graphs this Python runs at
+        capture only and the plan is baked in.
+        """
+        mono = self.mono
+        mono.active = False
+        if intermediate_tensors is not None or self._kv is None:
+            return None
+        if not is_forward_context_available():
+            return None
+        if get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE:
+            return None
+        kv = mla_cache(mono.layers[mono.first])
+        if (kv.data_ptr(), kv.numel()) != self._kv:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "GLM-5.2 specialized decode: the KV cache was re-bound without "
+                "prepare_kv (ModelState.initialize_kv_cache)"
+            )
+        S = mono.begin_step(positions)
+        return None if S is None else Step(positions.shape[0], S, self.kernels)
+
+    def after_step(self) -> None:
+        """Once per executed step, from compute_logits (runs eagerly on every rank, also
+        under graph replay). Raises on expired polls."""
+        if self.watch is not None and not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            self.watch.after_step()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Build-time checks and the poll-error fail-stop of the GLM-5.2 specialized decode
+(the config-only checks are ``runtime.unsupported``, the KV-bind checks
+``MonoLayers.bind_caches``).
+
+Build (``SpecializedDecode.__init__``): vLLM's RoPE cache covers max_model_len. Per step
+(``PollErrorWatch``): a non-blocking, one-step-delayed fail-stop on expired kernel
+polls, so the engine fails instead of serving wrong tokens."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def check_rope_table(backbone, cfg) -> None:
+    """VLLM's cos_sin_cache covers the kernel's RoPE table (cfg.max_model_len >= vLLM's
+    max_model_len, see ``runtime.decode_config``)."""
+    rows = backbone.layers[cfg.layers[0]].self_attn.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache.shape[0]
+    if rows < cfg.max_model_len:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"GLM-5.2 specialized decode: vLLM's cos_sin_cache has {rows} rows < "
+            f"max_model_len {cfg.max_model_len}"
+        )
+
+
+# the output rank's first fail-stop message (None until one fires)
+_FAILED: dict[str, str | None] = dict(msg=None)
+# seconds the output rank lives on after its fail-stop, for the raised error to reach
+# the engine through the worker's RPC reply
+FAILSTOP_EXIT_GRACE_S = 5.0
+
+
+def _fail_hard(msg: str):
+    """Terminate this worker: a non-output TP rank's exception never reaches the
+    engine, so raising would let the other ranks keep emitting tokens."""
+    logger.critical("%s -> terminating this worker (non-output rank)", msg)
+    os._exit(70)
+
+
+def _arm_exit_watchdog(grace_s: float = FAILSTOP_EXIT_GRACE_S):
+    """Exit this worker grace_s seconds from now, whatever its threads do: after a
+    fail-stop the engine has usually queued the next step, whose collectives wait on
+    the exited peers while the main thread spins in a device sync (no signal handling).
+    faulthandler's watchdog is a C thread (no GIL): it dumps every stack, then
+    _exit(1)s."""
+    import faulthandler
+
+    try:
+        faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(grace_s, exit=True, file=2)
+    except Exception:
+        import threading
+        import time
+
+        def _exit():
+            time.sleep(grace_s)
+            os._exit(70)
+
+        threading.Thread(target=_exit, daemon=True, name="MonoFailStopExit").start()
+
+
+def fail_stop(msg: str, rank: int):
+    """Terminate the worker on non-output ranks; on the output rank latch the first
+    fail-stop (arming the exit watchdog once) and raise."""
+    if rank != 0:
+        _fail_hard(msg)
+    msg = f"{msg} -> fail-stop"
+    if _FAILED["msg"] is None:
+        _FAILED["msg"] = msg
+        logger.error(
+            "%s -> the output rank raises; this worker exits in %.0f s (the other "
+            "ranks have exited, so it cannot run another step)",
+            msg,
+            FAILSTOP_EXIT_GRACE_S,
+        )
+        _arm_exit_watchdog()
+    raise RuntimeError(msg)
+
+
+class PollErrorWatch:
+    """One-step-delayed, non-blocking fail-stop on expired kernel polls (one async D2H
+    copy + event per step). Mode "raise": the output rank raises, the others exit;
+    "warn": log, count, clear the device words and continue."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mono):
+        from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.flydsl.glm.layout import (
+            POLL_STAGES,
+        )
+
+        self.mode = mono.cfg.failstop
+        self.rank = mono.rank
+        self.stages = POLL_STAGES
+        n = len(POLL_STAGES)
+        # (S, runtime index) -> device words
+        self.views, self.aborts, self.xviews = {}, {}, {}
+        self.steps = {}
+        for S in mono.batch_sizes:
+            for i, op in enumerate(mono.runtime_ops(S)):
+                off, oa = op.scr_layout["poll_err"], op.scr_layout["poll_abort"]
+                self.views[(S, i)] = op.scratch[off : off + 4 * n].view(torch.int32)
+                self.aborts[(S, i)] = op.scratch[oa : oa + 4].view(torch.int32)
+                # rank 0: the ranks that flagged an expired wait into its buffer
+                self.xviews[(S, i)] = op.poll_xrank
+                if i == 0:
+                    self.steps[S] = op.step
+        npes = max(v.numel() for v in self.xviews.values())
+        self.host = torch.zeros(len(self.views), n, dtype=torch.int32, pin_memory=True)
+        self.host_x = torch.zeros(
+            len(self.xviews), npes, dtype=torch.int32, pin_memory=True
+        )
+        # optional device non-finite counter (device_nonfinite + failstop_nonfinite)
+        nf = mono.dev_nonfinite if mono.cfg.failstop_nonfinite else None
+        self.nonfinite = nf
+        self.host_nf = (
+            None if nf is None else torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, pin_memory=True)
+        )
+        self.event: torch.cuda.Event | None = None
+        self.checks = 0
+        self.n_incidents = 0  # warn mode
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _describe(keys, bad, fmt) -> list:
+        out = set()
+        for i, j in bad:
+            S, rt = keys[i]
+            out.add(fmt(f"S{S}/rt{rt}" if rt else f"S{S}", j))
+        return sorted(out)
+
+    def _incident(self, what, kind="expired kernel polls"):
+        """Slow path only (an expiry happened): reads the abort marks / step counters
+        synchronously."""
+        marks = {
+            f"S{k[0]}/{k[1]}": int(v[0]) - 1
+            for k, v in self.aborts.items()
+            if int(v[0]) != 0
+        }
+        steps = {S: int(t[0]) for S, t in self.steps.items()}
+        msg = (
+            f"GLM-5.2 specialized decode rank {self.rank}: {kind} {what} (expired at "
+            f"kernel step {marks}; step counters now {steps}; check {self.checks}) -- "
+            "outputs of those steps are wrong"
+        )
+        if self.mode != "warn":
+            fail_stop(
+                f"{msg} (outputs since the previous check may be wrong)", self.rank
+            )
+        self.n_incidents += 1
+        logger.error(
+            "%s [failstop=warn: continuing, incident %d]",
+            msg,
+            self.n_incidents,
+        )
+        for v in (*self.views.values(), *self.aborts.values(), *self.xviews.values()):
+            v.zero_()
+        self.host.zero_()
+        self.host_x.zero_()
+
+    def after_step(self):
+        if self.event is not None and self.event.query():
+            self.checks += 1
+            bad = self.host.nonzero().tolist()
+            if bad:
+                stage = lambda w, j: f"{w}:{self.stages[j]}"
+                self._incident(self._describe(list(self.views), bad, stage))
+            bad = self.host_x.nonzero().tolist()
+            if bad:
+                peer = lambda w, j: f"rank{j}@{w}"
+                self._incident(
+                    self._describe(list(self.xviews), bad, peer),
+                    "expired kernel polls on peer",
+                )
+            if self.host_nf is not None and int(self.host_nf[0]) > 0:
+                n = int(self.host_nf[0])
+                if self.mode == "warn" and self.nonfinite is not None:
+                    self.nonfinite.zero_()
+                    self.host_nf.zero_()
+                self._incident(
+                    ["nonfinite"], f"{n} step(s) with non-finite hidden states"
+                )
+            self.event = None
+        if self.event is None:
+            for i, v in enumerate(self.views.values()):
+                self.host[i].copy_(v, non_blocking=True)
+            for i, v in enumerate(self.xviews.values()):
+                self.host_x[i].copy_(v, non_blocking=True)
+            if self.host_nf is not None:
+                self.host_nf.copy_(self.nonfinite, non_blocking=True)
+            self.event = torch.cuda.Event()
+            self.event.record()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Run only the sparse-attention indexer of a ``DeepseekV32MLAAttention`` layer (ROCm).
+
+Mirrors ``DeepseekV32MLAAttention.forward`` / ``_fused_attention`` (amd/rocm.py) up to
+``_run_indexer``: it writes the index-K cache and the shared top-k buffer, but passes
+``mla_kv_cache=None`` to ``fused_norm_rope`` (the MonoKernel writes the MLA row) and
+skips q_b_proj / W_UK / sparse MQA / W_UV / o_proj (``fused_q`` gets zero MQA dummies
+whose outputs are discarded).
+
+``trim=True`` (``DecodeConfig.indexer_trim``) drops discarded work without changing a
+value the indexer consumes: the MQA dummies become persistent zero buffers, and only the
+q_lora rows of ``fused_qkv_a_proj`` are computed (same linear method on a row-slice of
+the weight, kept per layer and row count only after a one-time bitwise self-check
+against the full GEMM; kv_c / k_pe then come from persistent dummies)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.amd.specialized_decode.runtime.mono_layers import (
+    layer_metadata,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v32.common.kernels import fused_norm_rope, fused_q
+
+
+def _dummy_shapes(attn) -> dict[str, tuple[int, ...]]:
+    h, r, kv = attn.num_local_heads, attn.qk_rope_head_dim, attn.kv_lora_rank
+    return dict(kv_c=(kv,), k_pe=(r,), q_pe=(h, r), ql_nope=(h, kv))
+
+
+class IndexerRefresh:
+    """The indexer-only refresh of one layer, with its trim-mode state: persistent zero
+    dummies (allocated here, before any graph capture) and, per row count, whether the
+    sliced q GEMM was verified bit-identical to the full one."""
+
+    def __init__(self, attn, rows: int, dtype, device, trim: bool = False):
+        assert attn.indexer is not None and not attn.skip_topk
+        self.attn, self.trim = attn, trim
+        self.shapes = _dummy_shapes(attn)
+        self.dummies: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+        # T -> True (sliced q GEMM verified bitwise) / False (keep the full GEMM)
+        self.q_slice_ok: dict[int, bool] = {}
+        if trim:
+            for name in self.shapes:
+                self._dummy(name, rows, dtype, device)
+
+    def _dummy(self, name, T, dtype, device) -> torch.Tensor:
+        buf = self.dummies.get(name)
+        if (
+            buf is None
+            or buf.shape[0] < T
+            or buf.dtype != dtype
+            or buf.device != device
+        ):
+            buf = torch.zeros(
+                (max(T, 16), *self.shapes[name]), dtype=dtype, device=device
+            )
+            self.dummies[name] = buf
+        return buf[:T]
+
+    def _q_rows(self, hidden_states):
+        """q_lora rows of fused_qkv_a_proj via a row-slice of its weight, or None unless
+        verified bit-identical to the full GEMM (then the caller runs the full GEMM)."""
+        attn = self.attn
+        lin = attn.fused_qkv_a_proj
+        T = hidden_states.shape[0]
+        ok = self.q_slice_ok.get(T)
+        if (
+            ok is False
+            or not hasattr(lin, "weight")
+            or getattr(lin, "_use_min_latency_gemm", False)
+        ):
+            return None
+        if (
+            ok is None
+            and torch.cuda.is_available()
+            and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+        ):
+            # the self-check syncs (warm-up runs verify each row count first)
+            return None
+        try:
+            w = lin.weight[: attn.q_lora_rank]
+            q = lin.quant_method.apply(SimpleNamespace(weight=w), hidden_states, None)
+        except Exception:  # the quant method needs more than .weight
+            self.q_slice_ok[T] = False
+            return None
+        if ok is None:
+            full = lin(hidden_states)[0][:, : attn.q_lora_rank]
+            self.q_slice_ok[T] = bool(torch.equal(q, full))
+            if not self.q_slice_ok[T]:
+                return None
+        return q
+
+    def __call__(self, positions: torch.Tensor, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        attn, trim = self.attn, self.trim
+        T, dev, dt = hidden_states.shape[0], hidden_states.device, hidden_states.dtype
+
+        def zeros(name):
+            if trim:
+                return self._dummy(name, T, dt, dev)
+            return torch.zeros(T, *self.shapes[name], dtype=dt, device=dev)
+
+        q_c = self._q_rows(hidden_states) if trim else None
+        if q_c is not None:
+            kv_c, k_pe = zeros("kv_c"), zeros("k_pe")
+        else:
+            qkv_lora = attn.fused_qkv_a_proj(hidden_states)[0]
+            q_c, kv_c, k_pe = qkv_lora.split(
+                [attn.q_lora_rank, attn.kv_lora_rank, attn.qk_rope_head_dim], dim=-1
+            )
+        kw = attn.indexer.wk_weights_proj(hidden_states)[0]
+        index_k = kw[:, : attn.indexer.head_dim]
+        index_weights = kw[:, attn.indexer.head_dim :]
+        md, mla_slot = layer_metadata(attn.layer_name)
+        assert md is not None, "indexer-only refresh needs attention metadata"
+
+        q_c = fused_norm_rope(
+            positions,
+            q_c,
+            attn.q_a_layernorm.weight,
+            attn.q_a_layernorm.variance_epsilon,
+            kv_c,
+            attn.kv_a_layernorm.weight,
+            attn.kv_a_layernorm.variance_epsilon,
+            k_pe,
+            attn.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache,
+            index_k,
+            attn.indexer.k_norm.weight,
+            attn.indexer.k_norm.bias,
+            attn.indexer.k_norm.eps,
+            attn.indexer_rope_emb.cos_sin_cache,
+            attn.topk_indices_buffer,
+            slot_mapping=mla_slot,
+            indexer_k_cache=attn.indexer.k_cache.kv_cache,
+            indexer_cache_shuffled=attn.indexer.k_cache.uses_shuffled_layout,
+            mla_kv_cache=None,  # MLA row is the MonoKernel's to write
+            mla_kv_cache_dtype=attn.kv_cache_dtype,
+            mla_k_scale=None,
+            has_indexer=True,
+            index_rope_interleave=attn._index_rope_interleave,
+        )
+        index_q = attn.indexer.wq_b(q_c)[0].view(
+            -1, attn.indexer.n_head, attn.indexer.head_dim
+        )
+        index_q_fp8, index_weights_out, _ = fused_q(
+            positions,
+            zeros("q_pe"),
+            attn.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache,
+            index_q,
+            attn.indexer_rope_emb.cos_sin_cache,
+            zeros("ql_nope"),
+            attn._q_scale,
+            index_weights,
+            attn.indexer.softmax_scale,
+            attn.indexer.n_head**-0.5,
+            has_indexer=True,
+            index_rope_interleave=attn._index_rope_interleave,
+            quantize_mqa=attn._fp8_kv,
+        )
+        attn._run_indexer(q_c, index_q_fp8, index_weights_out)
